sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第084卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 84.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 84.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀六】起重光作噩，盡玄黓閹茂，凡二年。

translations.literal: 【Jin Records 6】 From Chongguang Zuoe through Xuanque Yanmao—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Jin Records 6】 From the first year of the Chongguang cycle through the last year of the Xuanque cycle—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝中之上永寧元年（

translations.literal: Middle section of Emperor Xiaohui, upper part, first year of Yongning (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohui, middle reign, upper section, first year of Yongning (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元三零一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, 301 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou, 301 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以散騎常侍安定張軌為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Palace Attendant Zhang Gui of Anding was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Palace Attendant Zhang Gui of Anding was appointed governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 軌以時方多難，陰在保據河西之志，故求為涼州。

translations.literal: Gui, because the times were full of troubles, secretly harbored the ambition to secure and hold the Hexi region, and therefore requested Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was in turmoil, Gui secretly aimed to secure the Hexi corridor for himself and had sought the Liang post for that reason.

sentences.zh: 時州境盜賊縱橫，鮮卑為寇。

translations.literal: At the time bandits ranged across the province, and the Xianbei raided as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The province was overrun with bandits, and the Xianbei were raiding along the borders.

sentences.zh: 軌至，以宋配、汜瑗為謀主，悉討破之，威著西土。

translations.literal: When Gui arrived, he made Song Pei and Si Yuan his chief strategists, defeated them all, and his authority became renowned in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gui took office, he put Song Pei and Si Yuan in charge of planning, crushed every foe in turn, and his reputation spread throughout the west.

sentences.zh: 相國倫與孫秀使牙門趙奉詐傳宣帝神語云：「倫宜早入西宮。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Lun and Sun Xiu had gate officer Zhao Feng falsely transmit a divine message of Emperor Xuan, saying: "Lun ought to enter the Western Palace early."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Sima Lun and Sun Xiu had gate officer Zhao Feng spread a forged oracle of Emperor Xuan, saying, "Lun should enter the Western Palace at once."

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍義陽王威，望之孫也，素諂事倫，倫以威兼侍中，使威逼奪帝璽綬，作禪詔，又使尚書令滿奮持節、奉璽綬禪位於倫。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Prince of Yiyang Wei, grandson of Wang Wang, had long flattered and served Lun; Lun made Wei also Attendant-in-Ordinary and had Wei seize the emperor's seal and cord by force, draft the abdication edict, and further had Minister of Works Man Fen hold the staff of authority and present the seal and cord to abdicate the throne to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Sima Wei, Prince of Yiyang—a grandson of Wang Wang and a longtime flatterer of Lun—was made attendant-in-ordinary as well and ordered to wrest the imperial seal and cord from the emperor and draft the abdication edict. Lun then had Minister of Works Man Fen bear the staff of authority and present the regalia in formally yielding the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍王輿、前軍將軍司馬雅等帥甲士入殿，曉諭三部司馬，示以威賞，無敢違者。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Wang Yu, Forward Army General Sima Ya, and others led armored troops into the hall, announced and instructed the Three Departments' officials, displayed rewards and punishments, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Wang Yu, Forward Army General Sima Ya, and others marched armored troops into the hall, addressed the officials of the Three Departments, and made the rewards and penalties plain; no one dared resist.

sentences.zh: 張林等屯守諸門。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin and others garrisoned and guarded the various gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin and others held all the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，倫備法駕入宮，即帝位，赦天下，改元建始。

translations.literal: On yichou, Lun prepared the imperial chariot and entered the palace, assumed the imperial position, amnestied the realm, and changed the era name to Jianshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, Lun entered the palace in full imperial procession, took the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Jianshi.

sentences.zh: 帝自華林西門出居金墉城，倫使張衡將兵守之。

translations.literal: The emperor went out through the west gate of Hualin and took residence at Jincheng, and Lun had Zhang Heng lead troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sent out through the west gate of Hualin Park to live at Jincheng, and Lun stationed Zhang Heng with troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，尊帝為太上皇，改金墉曰永昌宮，廢皇太孫為濮陽王。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the emperor was honored as Retired Emperor, Jincheng was renamed Yongchang Palace, and the heir apparent was demoted to Prince of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, the emperor was styled Retired Emperor, Jincheng was renamed Yongchang Palace, and the heir apparent was demoted to Prince of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 立世子荂為皇太子，封子馥為京兆王，虔為廣平王，詡為霸城王，皆侍中將兵。

translations.literal: He established his heir Zan as crown prince, enfeoffed his son Fu as Prince of Jingzhao, Qian as Prince of Guangping, and Xu as Prince of Bacheng—all as attendants-in-ordinary commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: He named his heir Zan crown prince and enfeoffed his sons Fu as Prince of Jingzhao, Qian as Prince of Guangping, and Xu as Prince of Bacheng, each made attendant-in-ordinary with command of troops.

sentences.zh: 以梁王肜為宰衡，何劭為太宰，孫秀為侍中、中書監、驃騎將軍、儀同三司，義陽王威為中書令，張林為衛將軍，其餘黨與，皆為卿、將，超階越次，不可勝紀；

translations.literal: He appointed Prince of Liang Rong as Chief Minister, He Shao as Grand Tutor, Sun Xiu as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Cavalry General-in-Chief, and with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Yiyang Wei as Secretariat Director, Zhang Lin as Guard General; the rest of his faction were all made ministers and generals, promoted beyond rank and out of order, beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang Sima Rong was made chief minister, He Shao grand tutor, and Sun Xiu attendant-in-ordinary, director of the secretariat, cavalry general-in-chief, and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies; Sima Wei, Prince of Yiyang, became secretariat director and Zhang Lin guard general. Every other member of the clique was handed a ministerial or general's title, promoted far above his proper rank in numbers too great to list;

sentences.zh: 下至奴卒，亦加爵位。

translations.literal: down even to slaves and runners, ranks and titles were also added.
translations.idiomatic: even household slaves and runners were given noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，貂蟬盈坐，時人為之諺曰：「貂不足，狗尾續。」

translations.literal: At every court assembly, cicada and fox-tail insignia filled the seats, and people of the time made a proverb of it, saying: "When the martens are not enough, dog tails are added."
translations.idiomatic: At every court session the hall was packed with officials wearing cicada and fox-tail insignia, and contemporaries coined a saying: "When there are not enough sable tails, dog tails are sewn on."

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下所舉賢良、秀才、孝廉皆不試，郡國計吏及太學生年十六以上者皆署吏；

translations.literal: That year, all the worthy, cultivated talent, and filial and incorrupt nominees recommended throughout the realm were not examined; commandery and state accounting clerks and Imperial University students aged sixteen and above were all appointed officials;
translations.idiomatic: That year every worthy, cultivated-talent, and filial-and-incorrupt nominee in the empire was passed without examination; commandery and state accounting clerks and Imperial University students sixteen or older were all given official posts;

sentences.zh: 守令赦日在職者皆封侯；

translations.literal: prefects and magistrates who were in office on the amnesty day were all enfeoffed as marquises;
translations.idiomatic: every prefect and magistrate still in office on amnesty day was enfeoffed as a marquis;

sentences.zh: 郡綱紀並為孝廉，縣綱紀並為廉吏。

translations.literal: commandery chief clerks were all made filial and incorrupt nominees, and county chief clerks were all made incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: every commandery chief clerk was made a filial-and-incorrupt nominee and every county chief clerk an incorrupt official.

sentences.zh: 府庫之儲，不足以供賜與。

translations.literal: The stores of the treasury were insufficient to supply the bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury could not keep pace with the largesse.

sentences.zh: 應侯者多，鑄印不給，或以白板封之。

translations.literal: Those who were to receive marquisates were numerous; casting seals could not keep up, and some were enfeoffed with blank boards instead.
translations.idiomatic: So many men were being enfeoffed that the mint could not cast seals fast enough; some received blank boards in place of a proper seal.

sentences.zh: 初，平南將軍孫旂之子弼、弟子髦、輔、琰皆附會孫秀，與之合族，旬月間致位通顯。

translations.literal: Earlier, the sons of Pacifying South General Sun Qi—Bi—and his nephews Mao, Fu, and Yan had all attached themselves to Sun Xiu and merged clans with him; within a month or so they reached prominent positions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pacifying South General Sun Qi's son Bi and his nephews Mao, Fu, and Yan had all thrown in with Sun Xiu and been treated as one clan with him; within a month they had risen to conspicuous rank.

sentences.zh: 及倫稱帝，四子皆為將軍，封郡侯，以旂為車騎將軍、開府，旂以弼等受倫官爵過差，必為家禍，遣幼子回責之，弼等不從。

translations.literal: When Lun declared himself emperor, the four sons were all made generals and enfeoffed as commandery marquises; Qi was made Chariots and Cavalry General with an open office. Qi considered that Bi and the others had received offices and titles from Lun far beyond propriety and would surely bring disaster on the family; he sent his youngest son Hui to rebuke them, but Bi and the others would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun took the throne, all four were made generals and enfeoffed as commandery marquises, and Qi was appointed chariots-and-cavalry general with his own staff. Qi believed Bi and the others had accepted ranks from Lun far above their due and would ruin the family; he sent his youngest son Hui to rebuke them, but they refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 旂不能制，慟哭而已。

translations.literal: Qi could not control them and could only weep in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Qi could not restrain them and could only weep in despair.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，殺濮陽哀王臧。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Lamented Prince of Puyang Zang was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, Sima Zang, Lamented Prince of Puyang, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 孫秀專執朝政，倫所出詔令，秀輒改更與奪，自書青紙為詔，或朝行夕改，百官轉易如流。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu monopolized control of court affairs; edicts issued by Lun, Xiu would promptly alter, grant, or revoke. He himself wrote edicts on blue paper; some issued in the morning were changed by evening, and the hundred officials shifted like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu held the government in his own hands: every edict Lun issued, Xiu would rewrite, grant, or revoke at will. He drafted edicts himself on blue paper, sometimes replacing a morning order by evening, and official appointments changed as swiftly as a stream.

sentences.zh: 張林素與秀不相能，且怨不得開府，潛與太子荂箋，言：「秀專權不合眾心，而功臣皆小人，撓亂朝廷，可悉誅之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Lin had never gotten along with Xiu and moreover resented not receiving an open office; he secretly sent a letter to the crown prince Zan, saying: "Xiu monopolizes power and does not accord with popular sentiment, and the so-called meritorious men are all petty fellows who disrupt the court—they can all be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin had long been at odds with Xiu and also resented being denied an independent staff. He secretly wrote the crown prince Zan: "Xiu's monopoly on power has lost him the people's support, and his 'meritorious' followers are nothing but petty men sowing chaos at court—they should all be killed."

sentences.zh: 荂以書白倫，倫以示秀。

translations.literal: Zan reported the letter to Lun, and Lun showed it to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zan reported the letter to Lun, and Lun showed it to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 秀勸倫收林，殺之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Xiu urged Lun to arrest Lin, kill him, and exterminate his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu persuaded Lun to arrest Lin, execute him, and wipe out three generations of his family.

sentences.zh: 秀以齊王冏、成都王穎、河間王顒，各擁強兵，據方面，惡之。

translations.literal: Xiu regarded Prince of Qi Jiong, Prince of Chengdu Ying, and Prince of Hejian Yong, each holding strong armies and occupying a region, with hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu hated the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, and the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong, each of whom commanded large armies in his own territory.

sentences.zh: 乃盡用其親黨為三王參佐，加冏鎮東大將軍，穎征北大將軍，皆開府儀同三司，以寵安之。

translations.literal: He therefore entirely used his own kin and partisans as staff for the three princes, added to Jiong the title Pacifying East General-in-Chief and to Ying the title Campaigning North General-in-Chief, both with open offices and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, in order to favor and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore packed the three princes' staffs with his own kin and clients, gave Jiong the added title of pacifying-east general-in-chief and Ying that of campaigning-north general-in-chief, each with an open office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, hoping to buy their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李庠驍勇得眾心，趙廞浸忌之而未言。

translations.literal: Li Xiang was fierce and brave and won the hearts of the masses; Zhao Xin gradually came to resent him but did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang was a fierce fighter who had won the soldiers' loyalty, and Zhao Xin had begun to fear him but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 長史蜀郡杜淑、張粲說廞曰：「將軍起兵始爾，而遽遣李庠握強兵於外，非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Du Shu and Zhang Can of Shu Commandery said to Xin: "The general has only just raised his army, yet you hastily send Li Xiang to hold a strong force abroad; he is not of our kind, and his heart must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Du Shu and Zhang Can of Shu Commandery urged Xin: "You have only just begun this rising, yet you already send Li Xiang to command a large force in the field. He is not one of us, and his loyalty cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 此倒戈授人也，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: This is turning the blade and handing it to another; you should plot against him early."
translations.idiomatic: You would be putting a sword in an enemy's hand. Deal with him before it is too late."

sentences.zh: 會庠勸廞稱尊號，淑，粲因白廞以庠大逆不道，引斬之，並其子姪十餘人。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiang urged Xin to assume an imperial title; Shu and Can thereupon reported to Xin that Xiang had committed the greatest treason, had him led out and beheaded, together with more than ten of his sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang urged Xin to take an imperial title, Shu and Can denounced him for treason. Xin had him executed on the spot, along with more than ten sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 時李特、李流皆將兵在外，廞遣人慰撫之曰：「庠非所宜言，罪應死。

translations.literal: At the time Li Te and Li Liu were both commanding troops abroad; Xin sent men to console and reassure them, saying: "What Xiang said was not what he should have said; the crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te and Li Liu were both in the field at the time. Xin sent envoys to reassure them: "Xiang spoke out of turn and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 兄弟罪不相及。」

translations.literal: Brothers' crimes do not extend to one another."
translations.idiomatic: A brother's crime does not touch his kin."

sentences.zh: 復以特、流為督將。

translations.literal: He again appointed Te and Liu as supervising generals.
translations.idiomatic: He confirmed Te and Liu in their commands as supervising generals.

sentences.zh: 特、流怨廞，引兵歸綿竹。

translations.literal: Te and Liu resented Xin and led their troops back to Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Te and Liu were not appeased; they withdrew their troops to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 廞牙門將涪陵許弇求為巴東監軍，杜淑、張粲固執不許，弇怒，手殺淑、粲於廞閤閣下，淑、粲左右復殺弇。

translations.literal: Xin's gate general Xu Yan of Fuling requested to be overseer of the Ba-Dong army; Du Shu and Zhang Can obstinately refused permission. Yan in anger personally killed Shu and Can beneath the pavilion of Xin's headquarters; Shu and Can's attendants in turn killed Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's gate general Xu Yan of Fuling asked to be made overseer of the Ba-Dong army, but Du Shu and Zhang Can flatly refused. In a rage Yan killed Shu and Can with his own hand in the commander's hall; their guards then killed Yan in turn.

sentences.zh: 三人，皆廞之腹心也，廞由是遂衰。

translations.literal: All three were Xin's trusted intimates, and from this Xin declined.
translations.idiomatic: All three had been Xin's closest advisers, and from that moment his cause began to collapse.

sentences.zh: 廞遣長史犍為費遠、蜀郡太守李苾、督護常俊督萬餘人斷北道，屯綿竹之石亭。

translations.literal: Xin sent Chief Clerk Fei Yuan of Qianwei, Administrator of Shu Commandery Li Bi, and Supervisor Chang Jun to command more than ten thousand men to cut the northern route and encamp at Shiting in Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xin sent chief clerk Fei Yuan of Qianwei, Shu commandery administrator Li Bi, and supervisor Chang Jun with more than ten thousand men to block the northern road and camp at Shiting in Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 李特密收兵得七千餘人，夜襲遠等軍，燒之，死者什八九，遂進攻成都。

translations.literal: Li Te secretly gathered troops to more than seven thousand, attacked Yuan's army and the others by night, burned them, and eight or nine tenths of the dead fell on their side; he then advanced to attack Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te quietly mustered more than seven thousand men, struck Yuan's camp by night, and burned it; eight or nine men in ten were killed, and he marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 費遠、李苾及軍祭酒張微，夜斬關走，文武盡散。

translations.literal: Fei Yuan, Li Bi, and Army Libationer Zhang Wei cut through the passes by night and fled; civil and military officials all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yuan, Li Bi, and army libationer Zhang Wei broke out of the city by night and fled; the entire administration dissolved.

sentences.zh: 廞獨與妻子乘小船走，至廣都，為從者所殺。

translations.literal: Xin alone with his wife and children took a small boat and fled; when he reached Guangdu he was killed by his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Xin fled alone with his wife and children in a small boat, but when he reached Guangdu his own escort killed him.

sentences.zh: 特入成都，縱兵大掠，遣使詣洛陽，陳廞罪狀。

translations.literal: Te entered Chengdu, let his troops plunder on a great scale, and sent envoys to Luoyang to set forth Xin's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Te entered Chengdu, let his troops loot the city, and sent envoys to Luoyang listing Xin's crimes.

sentences.zh: 初，梁州刺史羅尚，聞趙廞反，表「廞素非雄才，蜀人不附，敗亡可計日而待。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Governor of Liang Province Luo Shang, hearing that Zhao Xin had rebelled, memorialized: "Xin has never been a heroic talent; the people of Shu do not attach to him—defeat and ruin can be awaited within countable days."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liang province governor Luo Shang heard that Zhao Xin had rebelled, he memorialized: "Xin was never a man of real ability, and the people of Shu will not follow him. His fall can be measured in days."

sentences.zh: 詔拜尚平西將軍、益州刺史，督牙門王敦、蜀郡太守徐儉，廣漢太守辛冉等七千餘人入蜀。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shang Pacifying West General and Inspector of Yi Province, directing Gate Officer Wang Dun, Administrator of Shu Commandery Xu Jian, Administrator of Guanghan Xin Ran, and more than seven thousand others to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Shang pacifying-west general and inspector of Yi province and sent him into Shu at the head of gate officer Wang Dun, Shu administrator Xu Jian, Guanghan administrator Xin Ran, and more than seven thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 特等聞尚來，甚懼，使其弟驤於道奉迎，並獻珍玩。

translations.literal: Te and the others, hearing that Shang was coming, were greatly afraid and had his younger brother Xiang meet and welcome him on the road, also presenting rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Te and his followers were alarmed when they heard Shang was coming. Te sent his brother Xiang ahead to welcome him on the road with costly gifts.

sentences.zh: 尚悅，以驤為騎督。

translations.literal: Shang was pleased and made Xiang Cavalry Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Shang was pleased and appointed Xiang cavalry supervisor.

sentences.zh: 特、流復以牛酒勞尚於綿竹，王敦、辛冉說尚曰：「特等專為盜賊，宜因會斬之；

translations.literal: Te and Liu again used oxen and wine to feast Shang at Mianzhu; Wang Dun and Xin Ran said to Shang: "Te and the others are nothing but bandits; you should take advantage of the occasion to behead them;
translations.idiomatic: Te and Liu again entertained Shang with beef and wine at Mianzhu. Wang Dun and Xin Ran urged him: "These men are nothing but bandits. Strike now while you have them together;

sentences.zh: 不然，必為後患。」

translations.literal: otherwise they will surely become a later calamity."
translations.idiomatic: or they will surely become a lasting scourge."

sentences.zh: 尚不從。

translations.literal: Shang did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shang refused.

sentences.zh: 冉與特有舊，謂特曰：「故人相逢，不吉當凶矣。」

translations.literal: Ran had old ties with Te and said to Te: "When old acquaintances meet, if it is not auspicious it will be ominous."
translations.idiomatic: Ran, who knew Te of old, told him: "When old friends meet again, fortune turns to misfortune."

sentences.zh: 特深自猜懼。

translations.literal: Te was deeply suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Te took the remark as a deadly warning and grew deeply fearful.

sentences.zh: 三月，尚至成都。

translations.literal: In the third month, Shang reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Shang entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 汶山羌反，尚遣王敦討之，為羌所殺。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Wenshan rebelled; Shang sent Wang Dun to suppress them, and he was killed by the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wenshan Qiang rose in revolt. Shang sent Wang Dun against them, and the Qiang killed him.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏謀討趙王倫，未發，會離狐王盛、穎川處穆聚眾於濁澤，百姓從之，日以萬數。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jiong was plotting to attack Prince of Zhao Lun but had not yet set out, when it happened that Wang Sheng of Lihu and Chu Mu of Yingchuan gathered crowds at Zhuo Marsh; the common people followed them, increasing by tens of thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi Sima Jiong was planning to move against the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun but had not yet marched when Wang Sheng of Lihu and Chu Mu of Yingchuan raised a host at Zhuo Marsh. Commoners flocked to them by the tens of thousands each day.

sentences.zh: 倫以其將管襲為齊王軍司，討盛、穆，斬之。

translations.literal: Lun made his general Guan Xi army supervisor for the Prince of Qi to attack Sheng and Mu and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent his general Guan Xi as army supervisor under the Prince of Qi's banner to crush Sheng and Mu and execute them.

sentences.zh: 冏因收襲，殺之，與豫州刺史何勖、龍驤將軍董艾等起兵，遣使告成都王穎、河間王顒、常山王乂及南中郎將新野公歆，移檄征、鎮、州、郡、肥、國，稱：「逆臣孫秀，迷誤趙王，當共誅討。

translations.literal: Jiong thereupon seized Xi and killed him, and with Inspector of Yu Province He Xu, Rapid-as-a-Dragon General Dong Ai, and others raised troops; he sent envoys to notify Prince of Chengdu Ying, Prince of Hejian Yong, Prince of Changshan Ai, and Southern Gentlemen-of-the-House Duke of Xinye Xin, and issued a proclamation to expeditionary forces, garrisons, provinces, commanderies, counties, and states, stating: "The rebellious minister Sun Xiu has led the Prince of Zhao astray; we should jointly punish and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong then arrested Xi and executed him, joined Inspector of Yu He Xu, Rapid-as-a-Dragon General Dong Ai, and others in raising an army, and sent envoys to the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong, the Prince of Changshan Sima Ai, and Southern Gentlemen-of-the-House Sima Xin, Duke of Xinye. His proclamation went out to every expeditionary force, garrison, province, commandery, county, and kingdom: "The traitor Sun Xiu has misled the Prince of Zhao. Let us destroy them together.

sentences.zh: 有不從命者，誅及三族。」

translations.literal: Whoever did not obey the command would have punishment extending to three clans."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who refused would have three generations of his family put to death."

sentences.zh: 使者至鄴，成都王穎召鄴令盧志謀之。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Ye, Prince of Chengdu Ying summoned Magistrate of Ye Lu Zhi to consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Ye, the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying summoned Ye magistrate Lu Zhi for counsel.

sentences.zh: 志曰：「趙王篡逆，人神共憤，殿下收英俊以從人望，杖大順以討之，百姓必不召自至，攘臂爭進，蔑不克矣！」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "The Prince of Zhao has usurped and rebelled; men and spirits alike are enraged. Your Highness should gather outstanding men to follow popular expectation, uphold the great mandate to attack him, and the common people will surely come without being summoned, rolling up their sleeves to vie in advancing—nothing will fail to be overcome!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said: "The Prince of Zhao has usurped the throne, and both men and gods are outraged. If Your Highness gathers the best talent to meet the people's hopes and marches under the banner of righteousness, the common folk will flock to you unbidden, eager to fight—and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 穎從之，以志為諮議參軍，仍補左長史。

translations.literal: Ying followed this, made Zhi Consulting Army Adjutant, and additionally appointed him Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Ying took his advice, made Zhi a consulting army adjutant, and also appointed him left chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 志，毓之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhi was the grandson of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was a grandson of Lu Yu.

sentences.zh: 穎以兗州刺史王彥、冀州刺史李毅、督護趙驤、石超等為前鋒，遠近響應；

translations.literal: Ying made Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan, Inspector of Ji Province Li Yi, Supervisors Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, and others his vanguard; near and far responded;
translations.idiomatic: Ying appointed Yan inspector Wang Yan, Ji inspector Li Yi, and supervisors Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao to lead his vanguard, and supporters rallied from every quarter;

sentences.zh: 至朝歌，眾二十餘萬。

translations.literal: when they reached Chaoge, the host was more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: by the time he reached Chaoge his force numbered more than two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 超，苞之孫也。

translations.literal: Chao was the grandson of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chao was a grandson of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 常山王乂在其國，與太原內史劉暾各帥眾為穎後繼。

translations.literal: Prince of Changshan Ai was in his state and, with Interior Minister of Taiyuan Liu Dun, each led forces as Ying's rear support.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan Sima Ai, in his own domain, and Taiyuan interior minister Liu Dun each led troops to follow in Ying's rear.

sentences.zh: 新野公歆得冏檄，未知所從。

translations.literal: Duke of Xinye Xin received Jiong's proclamation and did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xinye Sima Xin received Jiong's proclamation and could not decide which side to take.

sentences.zh: 嬖人王綏曰：「趙親而強，齊疏而弱，公宜從趙。」

translations.literal: His favorite Wang Sui said: "The Zhao prince is close kin and strong; the Qi prince is distant kin and weak—my lord ought to follow Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Wang Sui urged: "The Prince of Zhao is your close kinsman and holds the stronger hand; the Prince of Qi is more distant and weaker. You should side with Zhao."

sentences.zh: 參軍孫洵大言於眾曰：「趙王凶逆，天下當共誅之，何親疏強弱之有！」

translations.literal: Army Adjutant Sun Xun spoke loudly before the assembly: "The Prince of Zhao is vicious and rebellious; the realm should jointly execute him—what room is there for closeness, distance, strength, or weakness!"
translations.idiomatic: Army adjutant Sun Xun declared before the whole staff: "The Prince of Zhao is a villain and usurper. The empire must destroy him together. What does kinship or strength matter?"

sentences.zh: 歆乃從冏。

translations.literal: Xin thereupon followed Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then threw in with Jiong.

sentences.zh: 前安西參軍夏侯奭在始平，合眾數千人以應冏，遣使邀河間王顒。

translations.literal: Former Army Adjutant of Anxi Xia Hou Shi was at Shiping, gathered a host of several thousand to respond to Jiong, and sent envoys to invite Prince of Hejian Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Former Anxi army adjutant Xiahou Shi was at Shiping. He raised several thousand men to join Jiong and sent envoys urging the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong to do the same.

sentences.zh: 顒用長史隴西李含謀，遣振武將軍河間張方討擒奭及其黨，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Yong adopted the plan of Chief Clerk Li Han of Longxi, sent Quelling Martial General Zhang Fang of Hejian to attack and capture Shi and his faction, and had them cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Yong took the advice of chief clerk Li Han of Longxi and sent quelling-martial general Zhang Fang of Hejian to capture Shi and his followers, then had them cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 冏檄至，顒執冏使送於倫，遣張方將兵助倫。

translations.literal: When Jiong's proclamation arrived, Yong seized Jiong's envoy and sent him to Lun, and dispatched Zhang Fang to lead troops to aid Lun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's proclamation arrived, Yong arrested Jiong's envoy and sent him to Lun, then dispatched Zhang Fang with troops to reinforce Lun.

sentences.zh: 方至華陰，顒聞二王兵盛，復召方還，更附二王。

translations.literal: When Fang reached Huayin, Yong heard that the two princes' armies were strong, recalled Fang, and switched to attach to the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang reached Huayin, Yong heard how strong the two princes' armies had grown, recalled him, and switched sides to join them.

sentences.zh: 冏檄至揚州，州人皆欲應冏。

translations.literal: When Jiong's proclamation reached Yang Province, the people of the province all wished to respond to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's proclamation reached Yang province, everyone there wanted to rally to him.

sentences.zh: 刺史郗隆，慮之玄孫也，以兄子鑒及諸子悉在洛陽，疑未決，悉召僚吏謀之。

translations.literal: Inspector Chi Long, great-great-grandson of Chi Xu, because his brother's son Jian and all his sons were in Luoyang, was undecided in his doubts and summoned all his staff officers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Chi Long, a great-great-grandson of Chi Xu, hesitated because his nephew Jian and all his sons were hostages in Luoyang. He called his entire staff into council.

sentences.zh: 主簿淮南趙誘、前秀才虞潭皆曰：「趙王篡逆，海內所疾；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhao You of Huainan and former Cultivated Talent nominee Yu Tan both said: "The Prince of Zhao has usurped and rebelled; within the seas he is what all detest;
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhao You of Huainan and former cultivated-talent nominee Yu Tan both said: "The Prince of Zhao has usurped the throne, and the empire hates him for it.

sentences.zh: 今義兵四起，其敗必矣。

translations.literal: now righteous armies rise on every side—his defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous armies are rising everywhere. He is doomed.

sentences.zh: 為明使君計，莫若自將精兵，逕赴許昌，上策也；

translations.literal: for the enlightened envoy's planning, nothing is better than personally leading elite troops straight to Xuchang—the highest strategy;
translations.idiomatic: For Your Excellency, the best course is to lead your best troops yourself straight to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 遣將將兵會之，中策也；

translations.literal: to send a general to lead troops to join them is the middle strategy;
translations.idiomatic: The next best is to send a general with your army to join the coalition.

sentences.zh: 量遣小軍，隨形助勝，下策也。」

translations.literal: to measure out and send a small force to follow the situation and help secure victory is the lowest strategy."
translations.idiomatic: The worst is to send only a token force to tag along after victory is already in sight."

sentences.zh: 隆退，密與別駕顧彥謀之，彥曰：「誘等下策，乃上計也。」

translations.literal: Long withdrew and secretly consulted with Vice-Prefect Gu Yan; Yan said: "What You and the others called the lowest strategy is in fact the highest plan."
translations.idiomatic: Long withdrew and took counsel privately with vice-prefect Gu Yan, who said: "What Zhao You called the worst plan is actually the wisest."

sentences.zh: 治中留寶、主簿張褒、西曹留承聞之，請見，曰：「不審明使君今當何施？」

translations.literal: Administrator Liu Bao, Chief Clerk Zhang Bao, and Western Bureau Liu Cheng heard of this, requested an audience, and said: "We do not know what course the enlightened envoy intends to take now."
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Liu Bao, chief clerk Zhang Bao, and western bureau officer Liu Cheng heard of this, asked for an audience, and said: "We do not know what Your Excellency intends to do."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「我俱受二帝恩，無所偏助，欲守州而己。」

translations.literal: Long said: "I have received favor from both emperors alike and will favor neither side; I wish only to hold the province and that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Long replied: "I owe loyalty to both emperors and will take neither side. I mean only to hold this province."

sentences.zh: 承曰：「天下，世祖之天下也。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "The realm is the realm of Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 太上承代已久，今上取之，不平，齊王順時舉事，成敗可見。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor has borne the succession for long; the present emperor took it from him—this is unjust. The Prince of Qi acts in accord with the times; success or failure can already be seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor held the throne for years before the present ruler seized it from him—that was wrong. The Prince of Qi is acting with the times, and the outcome is already plain.

sentences.zh: 使君不早發兵應之，狐疑遷延，變難將生，此州豈可保也！」

translations.literal: If the envoy does not raise troops early to respond, but hesitates and delays, calamity will arise—how can this province be preserved!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Excellency does not march now, hesitation will bring disaster, and this province will not be safe."

sentences.zh: 隆不應。

translations.literal: Long did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Long gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 潭，翻之孫也。

translations.literal: Tan was the grandson of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan was a grandson of Yu Fan.

sentences.zh: 隆停檄六日不下，將士憤怒。

translations.literal: Long held the proclamation for six days without issuing a response; officers and soldiers were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Long sat on Jiong's proclamation for six days without acting, and his officers and men grew furious.

sentences.zh: 參軍王邃鎮石頭，將士爭往歸之，隆遣從事於牛渚禁之，不能止。

translations.literal: Army Adjutant Wang Sui garrisoned Stone City; officers and soldiers vied to go over to him. Long sent an aide to Niuzhu to forbid it but could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Army adjutant Wang Sui held Stone City, and troops rushed to join him. Long sent an aide to Niuzhu to stop them, but nothing could hold them back.

sentences.zh: 將士遂奉邃攻隆，隆父子及顧彥皆死，傳首於冏。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers thereupon supported Sui in attacking Long; Long, his sons, and Gu Yan all died, and their heads were sent to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: The troops then backed Sui in an attack on Long. Long, his sons, and Gu Yan were all killed, and their heads were sent to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍、監沔北諸軍事孟觀，以為紫宮帝坐無他變，倫必不敗，乃為之固守。

translations.literal: Pacifying South General and Supervisor of All Military Affairs North of the Mian, Meng Guan, considered that in the Purple Palace the imperial throne showed no other change and Lun would surely not be defeated, and therefore held firm for him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-south general and supervisor of military affairs north of the Han, Meng Guan, believed the astrological signs showed no change in the imperial seat and that Lun could not lose; he therefore stood firm on Lun's side.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀聞三王兵起，大懼，詐為冏表曰：「不知何賊猝見攻圍，臣懦弱不能自固，乞中軍見救，庶得歸死。」

translations.literal: Sima Lun and Sun Xiu heard the three princes had raised troops, were greatly afraid, and forged a memorial in Sima Jiong's name, saying: "I do not know what bandits suddenly appeared attacking and surrounding me; your servant is weak and cannot hold firm on his own, and begs the Central Army to come and rescue me so that I may return to die."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun and Sun Xiu learned that the three princes had taken the field, they were terrified. They forged a dispatch in Sima Jiong's name: "Bandits of unknown origin have suddenly besieged me. I am too weak to hold my position and beg the Central Army to relieve me, that I may at least die in my own command."

sentences.zh: 以其表宣示內外；

translations.literal: They displayed this memorial within and without;
translations.idiomatic: They published the forged memorial throughout the court and the capital;

sentences.zh: 遣上軍將軍孫輔、折衝將軍李嚴帥兵七千自廷壽關出，征虜將軍張泓、左軍將軍蔡璜、前軍將軍閭和帥兵九千自崿阪關出，鎮軍將軍司馬雅、揚威將軍莫原帥兵八千自成皋關出，以拒冏。

translations.literal: they sent Upper Army General Sun Fu, Break-the-Ranks General Li Yan leading seven thousand troops out through Yanshou Pass, Captive-quelling General Zhang Hong, Left Army General Cai Huang, and Forward Army General Lü He leading nine thousand out through Eban Pass, Garrison Army General Sima Ya and Display Might General Mo Yuan leading eight thousand out through Chenggao Pass, to resist Sima Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: they sent Upper Army general Sun Fu and Break-the-Ranks general Li Yan with seven thousand men through Yanshou Pass; Zhang Hong, Cai Huang, and Lü He with nine thousand through Eban Pass; and Sima Ya and Mo Yuan with eight thousand through Chenggao Pass—all to block Sima Jiong.

sentences.zh: 遣孫秀子會督將軍士猗、許超帥宿衛兵三萬以拒穎。

translations.literal: They sent Sun Xiu's son Sun Hui, supervising generals Shi Yi and Xu Chao leading thirty thousand palace guards to resist Sima Ying.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Sun Xiu's son Sun Hui, with Shi Yi and Xu Chao supervising, at the head of thirty thousand imperial guards to hold off Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 召東平王楙為衛將軍，都督諸軍，又遣京兆王馥、廣平王虔帥兵八千為三軍繼援。

translations.literal: They summoned the Prince of Dongping Mao as Defender General, supervising all armies, and also sent the Prince of Jingzhao Fu and the Prince of Guangping Qian each leading eight thousand as three-army follow-up reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: They recalled the Prince of Dongping, Mao, as Defender General to command all forces, and sent the Princes of Jingzhao and Guangping, Fu and Qian, each with eight thousand men as a second echelon for the three field armies.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀日夜禱祈、厭勝以求福，使巫覡選戰日，又使人於嵩山著羽衣，詐稱仙人王喬，作書述倫祚長久，欲以惑眾。

translations.literal: Sima Lun and Sun Xiu day and night prayed and used sorcery to seek fortune, had shamans choose battle days, and also sent someone to Mount Song in feather robes falsely claiming to be the immortal Wang Qiao, composing a document stating Sima Lun's reign would be long-lasting, intending to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun and Sun Xiu prayed day and night and resorted to occult rites for luck. Shamans were told to pick auspicious battle days; a man was sent to Mount Song in immortal's robes to impersonate Wang Qiao and circulate writings promising a long reign for Lun, all to deceive the people.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day of bingxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the new moon of bingxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 自正月至於是月，五星互經天，縱橫無常。

translations.literal: From the first month until this month, the five planets repeatedly crossed the heavens, wandering irregularly.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month through this one, the five planets crossed the sky again and again in erratic paths.

sentences.zh: 張泓等進據陽翟，與齊王冏戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hong and others advanced and held Yangzhai, fought with the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong advanced and seized Yangzhai, then fought Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, defeating him again and again.

sentences.zh: 冏軍穎陰，夏，四月，泓乘勝逼之，冏遣兵逆戰。

translations.literal: Sima Jiong's army was at Yingyin; in summer, the fourth month, Hong pressed his advantage toward him, and Sima Jiong sent troops to meet him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong held Yingyin. In summer, the fourth month, Hong pressed the advantage; Jiong sent troops out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 諸軍不動，而孫輔、徐建軍夜亂，逕歸洛自首曰：「齊王兵盛，不可當，泓等已沒矣！」

translations.literal: The various armies did not move, but Sun Fu's and Xu Jian's armies rioted by night, went straight back to Luo to surrender themselves, saying: "The Prince of Qi's troops are numerous and cannot be withstood; Hong and the others are already lost!"
translations.idiomatic: The main armies held their ground, but Sun Fu's and Xu Jian's columns mutinied at night, fled straight to Luoyang, and reported: "The Prince of Qi's force is overwhelming—we cannot stand against it. Hong and the rest are already destroyed!"

sentences.zh: 趙王倫大恐，秘之，而召其子虔及許超還。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao Sima Lun was greatly afraid, kept it secret, and summoned back his son Qian and Xu Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, was terrified. He suppressed the report and recalled his son Qian and Xu Chao.

sentences.zh: 會泓破冏露布至，倫乃復遣之。

translations.literal: When Hong's bulletin of defeating Sima Jiong arrived, Sima Lun then sent him out again.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong's victory dispatch against Jiong arrived, Lun sent him back to the front.

sentences.zh: 泓等悉帥諸軍濟穎攻冏營，冏出兵擊其別將孫髦、司馬譚等，破之，泓等乃退。

translations.literal: Hong and the others all led the armies across the Ying to attack Sima Jiong's camp; Sima Jiong sent troops to strike their subordinate generals Sun Mao, Sima Tan, and others, defeating them, and Hong and the others then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hong led the whole force across the Ying to storm Jiong's camp. Jiong sallied out against subordinates Sun Mao and Sima Tan, routed them, and Hong pulled back.

sentences.zh: 孫秀詐稱已破冏營，擒得冏，令百官皆賀。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu falsely declared he had already broken Sima Jiong's camp and captured Sima Jiong, and ordered all officials to congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu falsely announced that Jiong's camp had been taken and Jiong captured, and ordered the whole bureaucracy to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎前鋒至黃橋，為孫會、士猗、許超所敗，殺傷萬餘人，士眾震駭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying's vanguard reached Huangqiao and was defeated by Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao, with more than ten thousand killed and wounded; officers and soldiers were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying's vanguard reached Huangqiao and was crushed by Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao. More than ten thousand were killed or wounded, and his army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 穎欲退保朝歌，盧志、王彥曰：「今我軍失利，敵新得志，有輕我之心。

translations.literal: Sima Ying wished to withdraw and hold Chaoge; Lu Zhi and Wang Yan said: "Now our army has suffered defeat; the enemy has newly gained success and has a mind to look down on us.
translations.idiomatic: Ying wanted to fall back on Chaoge. Lu Zhi and Wang Yan said: "We have just lost a battle. The enemy is fresh from victory and will take us lightly.

sentences.zh: 我若退縮，士氣沮衄，不可復用。

translations.literal: If we shrink back, morale will be crushed and broken and cannot be used again.
translations.idiomatic: If we retreat now, morale will collapse and these troops will never fight well again.

sentences.zh: 且戰何能無勝負！

translations.literal: Besides, in battle how can there be no victory or defeat!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, no battle is won every time!

sentences.zh: 不若更選精兵，星行倍道，出敵不意，此用兵之奇也。」

translations.literal: Better to select elite troops again, march by night doubling the stages, strike where the enemy does not expect—this is the marvel of employing troops."
translations.idiomatic: Better to pick a fresh elite force, march by night at double speed, and strike where they do not expect us—that is the classic surprise attack."

sentences.zh: 穎從之。

translations.literal: Sima Ying followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Ying took their advice.

sentences.zh: 倫賞黃橋之功，士猗、許超與孫會皆持節，由是各不相從，軍政不一，且恃勝輕穎而不設備。

translations.literal: Sima Lun rewarded the achievement at Huangqiao; Shi Yi, Xu Chao, and Sun Hui all held staffs of authority, and for this reason each did not follow the other, military and civil affairs were not unified, and moreover relying on victory they looked down on Sima Ying and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Lun rewarded the victors at Huangqiao. Shi Yi, Xu Chao, and Sun Hui each held independent command authority, so they would not coordinate; civil and military orders diverged, and flushed with victory they despised Ying and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 穎帥諸軍擊之，大戰於湨水，會等大敗，棄軍南走。

translations.literal: Sima Ying led the armies to strike them; a great battle was fought on the Zhu River; Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned their armies fleeing south.
translations.idiomatic: Ying led his host against them. At the Zhu River they fought a great battle; Hui and his colleagues were routed and fled south, abandoning their army.

sentences.zh: 穎乘勝長驅濟河。

translations.literal: Sima Ying pursued victory in long drive crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pressed the victory in a long pursuit across the river.

sentences.zh: 自冏等起兵，百官將士皆欲誅倫、秀，秀懼，不敢出中書省；

translations.literal: From the time Sima Jiong and the others raised troops, all officials and officers wished to execute Sima Lun and Sun Xiu; Sun Xiu was afraid and dared not leave the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Jiong and the others had risen, officials and soldiers alike wanted Lun and Xiu dead. Xiu was afraid to step outside the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 及聞河北軍敗，憂懣不知所為。

translations.literal: when he heard the Hebei army had been defeated, he was distressed and confused and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: when news came that the northern army had been beaten, he was frantic and could think of nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 孫會、許超、士猗等至，與秀謀。

translations.literal: Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, and the others arrived and plotted with Sun Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, Xu Chao, and Shi Yi arrived and held council with Xiu.

sentences.zh: 或欲收餘卒出戰；

translations.literal: Some wished to gather the remaining troops and go out to battle;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged rallying the survivors for one more battle;

sentences.zh: 或欲焚宮室，誅不附己者，挾倫南就孫旂、孟觀；

translations.literal: some wished to burn the palace halls, execute those not attached to themselves, and escort Sima Lun south to join Sun Qi and Meng Guan;
translations.idiomatic: some proposed burning the palace, killing everyone who would not follow them, and escorting Lun south to Sun Qi and Meng Guan;

sentences.zh: 或欲乘船東走入海，計未決。

translations.literal: some wished to take a boat and flee east into the sea; the plan was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: some wanted to take ship and flee east to the sea. No plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，左衛將軍王輿與尚書陵公漼帥營兵七百餘人，自南掖門入宮，三部司馬為應於內，攻孫秀、許超、士猗於中書省，皆斬之，遂殺孫奇、孫弼及前將軍謝惔等，漼，人由之子也。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Left Guard General Wang Yu and Minister-in-ordinary the Duke of Ling Cui led more than seven hundred camp soldiers, entered the palace from the Southern Flank Gate, the three department Simas responding inside, attacked Sun Xiu, Xu Chao, and Shi Yi in the Secretariat, and all were beheaded; they then killed Sun Qi, Sun Bi, and former Forward Army General Xie Yan and others—Cui was the son of Ren You.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Left Guard general Wang Yu and the Duke of Ling, Cui, a minister of the Secretariat, led just over seven hundred garrison troops in through the Southern Flank Gate while the three department Simas rose inside. They struck Sun Xiu, Xu Chao, and Shi Yi in the Secretariat and beheaded them all, then killed Sun Qi, Sun Bi, and former Forward Army general Xie Yan. Cui was a son of Ren You.

sentences.zh: 王輿屯雲龍門，召八坐皆入殿中，使倫為詔曰：「吾為孫秀所誤，以怒三王，今已誅秀。

translations.literal: Wang Yu stationed at the Cloud Dragon Gate, summoned all eight ministers into the hall, and had Sima Lun issue an edict saying: "I was misled by Sun Xiu and thereby angered the three princes; Sun Xiu has now been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu held the Cloud Dragon Gate, called in the eight chief ministers, and had Lun issue an edict: "Sun Xiu misled me and provoked the three princes. Xiu is now dead.

sentences.zh: 其迎太上皇復位，吾歸老於農畝。」

translations.literal: Welcome the Retired Emperor to restore the throne; I shall retire to farming in the fields."
translations.idiomatic: Welcome the Retired Emperor back to the throne. I will retire to the fields."

sentences.zh: 傳詔以騶虞幡敕將士解兵。

translations.literal: The edict was transmitted using the zouyu banner to order officers and soldiers to lay down arms.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was carried forth on the zouyu banner, ordering all troops to disarm.

sentences.zh: 黃門將倫自華林東門出，及太子荂皆還汶陽裡第，遣甲士數千迎帝於金墉城。

translations.literal: The yellow gate guard escorted Sima Lun out from the Eastern Gate of Huailin, and the crown prince Fen also, both returning to their residence at Wenyang Lane; thousands of armored soldiers were sent to welcome the emperor from Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate guards led Lun out through the east gate of Hualin Park; the crown prince Fen went with him back to Wenyang Lane. Thousands of armored men were sent to bring the emperor from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 百姓咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The common people all cried "ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The people shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 帝自端門入，升殿，群臣頓首謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor entered from the Duan Gate, ascended the hall, and the ministers all kowtowed begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered through the Duan Gate, took the throne, and the ministers kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 詔送倫、荂付金墉城。

translations.literal: An edict sent Sima Lun and Fen to be imprisoned at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Lun and Fen to be held at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 廣平王虔自河北還，至九曲，聞變，棄軍，將數十人歸裡第。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping Qian returned from Hebei; when he reached Jiuqu he heard of the change, abandoned his army, and with several tens of men returned to his home residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, Qian, was marching back from the north. At Jiuqu he heard what had happened, abandoned his army, and rode home with only a few dozen followers.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，赦天下，改元，大酺五日，分遣使者慰勞三王。

translations.literal: On guihai, amnesty was declared for all under heaven, the era name was changed, great feasting for five days, and envoys were dispatched separately to comfort and reward the three princes.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the empire was amnestied, the era name changed, and the court feasted for five days. Envoys were sent separately to congratulate the three princes.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜等表：「趙王倫父子凶逆，宜伏誅。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong and others memorialized: "The Prince of Zhao Sima Lun, father and sons, are vicious and rebellious and ought to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, and others memorialized: "Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, and his sons are traitors who deserve death."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣尚書袁敞持節賜倫死，收其子荂、馥、虔、詡，皆誅之。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Grand Master of Documents Yuan Chang was sent bearing the staff to grant Sima Lun death; his sons Fen, Fu, Qian, and Xu were arrested and all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yuan Chang of the Secretariat was sent with the imperial staff to grant Lun death. His sons Fen, Fu, Qian, and Xu were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 凡百官為倫所用者皆斥免，台、省、府、衛，僅有存者，是日，成都王穎至。

translations.literal: All officials whom Sima Lun had employed were dismissed; of the Secretariat, ministries, offices, and guards scarcely any remained—on that day the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Every official Lun had appointed was dismissed. Of the central offices and guards almost no one remained in post. That same day Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 己巳，河間王顒至。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, arrived.

sentences.zh: 穎使趙驤、石超助齊王冏討張泓等於陽翟，泓等皆降。

translations.literal: Sima Ying sent Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao to assist the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong in attacking Zhang Hong and the others at Yangzhai; Hong and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao to help Jiong finish off Zhang Hong at Yangzhai. Hong and his command surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自兵興六十餘日，戰鬥死者近十萬人。

translations.literal: From the rising of troops for more than sixty days, those who died in battle approached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting had lasted more than sixty days; nearly a hundred thousand had died in battle.

sentences.zh: 斬張衡、閭和、孫髦於東市，蔡璜自殺。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, Lü He, and Sun Mao were beheaded at the Eastern Market; Cai Huang killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, Lü He, and Sun Mao were beheaded at the Eastern Market. Cai Huang took his own life.

sentences.zh: 五月，誅議陽王威。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Prince of Yiyang Wei was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Sima Wei, Prince of Yiyang, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守宗岱承冏檄斬孫旂，永饒冶令空桐機斬孟觀，皆傳首洛陽，夷三族。

translations.literal: Xiangyang Administrator Zong Dai carried out Sima Jiong's order and beheaded Sun Qi; Yongrao magistrate Kongtong Ji beheaded Meng Guan; all sent heads to Luoyang and exterminated the three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang prefect Zong Dai, acting on Jiong's warrant, beheaded Sun Qi; Yongrao magistrate Kongtong Ji beheaded Meng Guan. Their heads were sent to Luoyang and all three men's clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 立襄陽王尚為皇太孫。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangyang Shang was established as imperial great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangyang, Shang, was named imperial great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙卯，齊王冏帥眾入洛陽，頓軍通章署，甲士數十萬，威震京都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yimao, the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong led the masses into Luoyang, encamped at the Tongzhang office, armored soldiers numbering hundreds of thousands, awe-shaking the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yimao, Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, entered Luoyang at the head of his host and camped at the Tongzhang offices with hundreds of thousands of armored men, dominating the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，赦天下。

translations.literal: On wuchen, amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the empire was amnestied again.

sentences.zh: 復封賓徒王晏為吳王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Bintu Yan was again enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan, Prince of Bintu, was reinstated as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔以齊王冏為大司馬，加九錫，備物典策，如宣、景、文、武輔魏故事；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict made the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong Grand Marshal, with the Nine Bestowals, full ritual objects and patent of investiture, following the precedent of Xuan, Jing, Wen, and Wu assisting Wei;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict named Jiong Grand Marshal with the Nine Bestowals, full ritual regalia and written patent, on the model of the great ministers who had assisted Cao Wei;

sentences.zh: 成都王穎為大將軍，都督中外諸軍事，假黃鉞，錄尚書事，加九錫，入朝不趨，劍履上殿；

translations.literal: the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying as Grand General, supervising all military affairs within and without, with the yellow battle-axe, recording Secretariat affairs, with the Nine Bestowals, not required to hasten on entering court, sword and shoes in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Ying as Grand General supervising all armies at home and abroad, with the yellow battle-axe, control of Secretariat affairs, the Nine Bestowals, exemption from hurrying at court, and permission to wear sword and shoes in the throne hall;

sentences.zh: 河間王顒為侍中、太尉，加三賜之禮；

translations.literal: the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong as Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Commandant, with the rites of the three bestowals;
translations.idiomatic: Yong as Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Commandant with the honors of the three bestowals;

sentences.zh: 常山王乂為撫軍大將軍，領左軍。

translations.literal: the Prince of Changshan Sima Yi as Pacification Army Grand General, commanding the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: and Yi, Prince of Changshan, as Pacification Army Grand General commanding the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 進廣陵公漼爵為王，領尚書，加侍中；

translations.literal: Duke of Guangling Cui was advanced in rank to prince, holding the Secretariat and added as Attendant-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Guangling Cui was raised to prince, put in charge of the Secretariat, and made Attendant-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 進新野公歆爵為王，都督荊州諸軍事，加鎮南大將軍。

translations.literal: Duke of Xinye Xin was advanced to prince, commanding all military affairs of Jing province, added as Pacification South Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: and Duke of Xinye Xin was raised to prince, made commander of all military affairs in Jing province, and named Pacification South Grand General.

sentences.zh: 齊、成都、河間三府，各置掾屬四十人，武號森列，文官備員而已，識者知兵之未戢也。

translations.literal: The three mansions of Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian each established forty staff members; military titles stood dense in ranks, civil offices merely filled quota—those with discernment knew warfare had not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The three princely establishments of Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian each took on forty staff officers. Military titles crowded the rolls while civil posts were mere placeholders—anyone with judgment could see the war was not over.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以梁王肜為太宰，領司徒。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Prince of Liang Sima Rong was made Grand Mentor, holding the post of Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, was made Grand Mentor and also Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉蕃女為趙世子荂妻，故蕃及二子散騎侍朗輿、冠軍將軍琨皆為趙王倫所委任。

translations.literal: Minister-in-ordinary Liu Fan's daughter was wife to the Heir of Zhao Fen; therefore Fan and his two sons Petitioned Within Regular Attendant Yu and Champion General Kun were all entrusted by the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan, a minister of the palace, had given his daughter to Lun's heir Fen in marriage, so Fan and his sons Yu and Kun had all been trusted appointees of Lun.

sentences.zh: 大司馬冏以琨父子有才望，特宥之，以輿為中書朗，琨為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Sima Jiong, because the Kun father and sons had talent and renown, specially pardoned them, appointing Yu as Secretariat Lang and Kun as Left Assistant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Jiong spared the Kun family for their reputation and talent, making Yu a secretariat officer and Kun left assistant director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又以前司徒王戎為尚書令，劉暾為御史中丞，王衍為河南尹。

translations.literal: Also the former Grand Steward Wang Rong as Secretariat Director, Liu Dan as Imperial Censor, Wang Yan as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He also named the former Grand Steward Wang Rong Secretariat Director, Liu Dan imperial censor, and Wang Yan intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 新野王歆將之鎮，與冏同乘謁陵，因說冏曰：「成都王至親，同建大勳，今宜留之與輔政；

translations.literal: The Prince of Xinye Xin was about to go to his post; riding with Sima Jiong he paid respects at the imperial tombs, and thereby advised Sima Jiong saying: "The Prince of Chengdu is close kin, together built the great achievement—now he ought to be kept to assist in government;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin, Prince of Xinye, was leaving for his post. He rode with Jiong to the imperial tombs and urged him: "Ying is your close kinsman and helped win this war. Keep him in the capital to share power;

sentences.zh: 若不能爾，當奪其兵權。」

translations.literal: if this cannot be done, his military authority ought to be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: if you will not do that, strip him of his troops."

sentences.zh: 常山王乂與成都王穎俱拜陵，乂謂穎曰：「天下者，先帝之業，王宜維正之。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan Sima Yi together with the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying paid respects at the tombs; Sima Yi said to Sima Ying: "The realm is the late emperor's enterprise; Your Highness ought to uphold and correct it."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan, and Ying both paid their respects at the tombs. Yi told Ying: "The realm is our late father's legacy. You ought to set it right."

sentences.zh: 聞其言者莫不憂懼。

translations.literal: Those who heard these words were none without worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who overheard him was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 盧志謂穎曰：「齊王眾號百萬，與張泓等相持不能決；

translations.literal: Lu Zhi said to Sima Ying: "The Prince of Qi is proclaimed at a million but could not decide matters with Zhang Hong and the others at Yangzhai;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi told Ying: "Jiong claims a million men yet could not finish Zhang Hong at Yangzhai;

sentences.zh: 大王逕前濟河，功無與貳。

translations.literal: Your Highness went straight forward crossing the river—achievement without a second.
translations.idiomatic: you crossed the river and won the war almost alone.

sentences.zh: 然今齊王欲與大王共輔朝政。

translations.literal: Yet now the Prince of Qi wishes to share with Your Highness in assisting court government.
translations.idiomatic: Now he wants you to share power at court.

sentences.zh: 志聞兩雄不俱立，宜因太妃微疾，求還定省，委重齊王，以收四海之心，此計之上也。」

translations.literal: I have heard two heroes cannot stand together; it is fitting to use the Princess Dowager's slight illness to request return to attend her, entrusting weighty matters to the Prince of Qi, thereby winning the hearts of all within the seas—this plan is tops."
translations.idiomatic: Two strong men cannot rule one court. Use your mother's slight illness as an excuse to go home and leave Jiong in charge. You will win the empire's goodwill—that is the best move."

sentences.zh: 穎從之。

translations.literal: Sima Ying followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Ying agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝見穎於東堂，慰勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Sima Ying in the Eastern Hall and comforted and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Ying in the Eastern Hall and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 穎拜謝曰：「此大司馬冏之勳，臣無豫焉。」

translations.literal: Sima Ying bowed in thanks saying: "This is Grand Marshal Sima Jiong's achievement; your servant had no part in it."
translations.idiomatic: Ying bowed and said: "This victory belongs to Grand Marshal Jiong. I had no part in it."

sentences.zh: 因表稱冏功德，宜委以萬機，自陳母疾，請歸籓。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial praising Sima Jiong's merit and virtue, saying he ought to be entrusted with the myriad affairs; he stated his own mother's illness and requested return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that Jiong's merit entitled him to full control of government, cited his mother's illness, and asked to return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 即辭出，不復還營，便謁太廟，出自東陽城門，遂歸鄴。

translations.literal: He immediately took leave and did not return to camp, but paid respects at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, went out from the Eastern Yang Gate, and then returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He left at once without returning to camp, paid respects at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, went out through the Eastern Yang Gate, and rode for Ye.

sentences.zh: 遣信與冏別，冏大驚，馳出送穎，至七里澗，及之。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to take leave of Sima Jiong; Sima Jiong was greatly alarmed, galloped out to escort Sima Ying, reaching Qili Ravine and catching up.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to take leave of Jiong. Jiong was stunned, galloped out after him, and caught up at Qili Ravine.

sentences.zh: 穎住車言別，流涕滂沱，惟以太妃疾苦為憂，不及時事。

translations.literal: Sima Ying stopped his carriage to speak farewell; tears poured down in torrents, concerned only for the Princess Dowager's illness, not touching on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ying halted his carriage for a last farewell, weeping freely, speaking only of his mother's illness and not a word of politics.

sentences.zh: 由是士民之譽皆歸穎。

translations.literal: For this reason the reputations of scholars and commoners all turned to Sima Ying.
translations.idiomatic: From that day public praise flowed to Ying.

sentences.zh: 冏辟新興劉殷為軍諮祭酒，洛陽令曹攄為記室督，尚書郎江統、陽平太守河內苟晞參軍事，吳國張翰為東曹掾，孫惠為戶曹掾，前廷尉正顧榮及順陽王豹為主簿。

translations.literal: Sima Jiong appointed the new Xingliu Liu Yin as Army Adviser Sacrificial Officer, Luoyang Magistrate Cao Shuai as Secretariat Supervisor, Secretariat Lang Jiang Tong and Former Interior Minister of Hanoi Gou Xi as military advisers, Wu's Zhang Han as Eastern Bureau clerk, Sun Hui as Household Bureau clerk, former Director of Justice Gu Rong and Prince of Shunyang Bao as chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong recruited Liu Yin of Xingliu as army adviser, Luoyang magistrate Cao Shuai as secretariat supervisor, Jiang Tong and former interior minister of Hanoi Gou Xi as staff officers, Zhang Han of Wu as eastern bureau clerk, Sun Hui as household bureau clerk, and former director of justice Gu Rong and the Prince of Shunyang, Bao, as chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 惠，賁之曾孫；

translations.literal: Hui was the great-grandson of Fen;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui was a great-grandson of Sun Fen;

sentences.zh: 榮，雍之孫也。

translations.literal: Rong was the grandson of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong was a grandson of Gu Yong.

sentences.zh: 殷幼孤貧，養曾祖母，以孝聞，人以谷帛遺之，殷受而不謝，直云：「待後貴當相酬耳。」

translations.literal: Yin from youth was orphaned and poor, reared his great-grandmother, famed for filial piety; when people gave him grain and cloth as gifts, Yin accepted but did not thank them, saying plainly: "Wait until later when I am noble and I shall repay you."
translations.idiomatic: Yin had been orphaned young and poor. He raised his great-grandmother and was known for filial piety. When neighbors gave him grain or cloth he accepted without thanks, saying only: "When I am rich I will repay you."

sentences.zh: 及長，博通經史，性倜儻有大志，儉而不陋，清而不介，望之頹然而不可侵也。

translations.literal: When grown, broadly mastered the classics and histories, by nature unconventional with great ambition, frugal yet not shabby, pure yet not aloof—one gazed at him as if drooping yet could not encroach on him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the classics and histories, was bold and ambitious, frugal without meanness, upright without harshness—people saw a relaxed man they dared not slight.

sentences.zh: 冏以何勖為中領軍，董艾典樞機，又封其將佐有功者葛旟、路秀、衛毅、劉真、韓泰皆為縣公，委以心膂，號曰「五公」。

translations.literal: Sima Jiong made He Xun Central Army Commander, Dong Ai in charge of the pivot, and also enfeoffed his generals and aides with achievement—Ge Yang, Lu Xiu, Wei Yi, Liu Zhen, Han Tai—all as dukes of counties, entrusting them as his inner core, styled the "Five Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong made He Xun central army commander and Dong Ai keeper of the keys. He enfeoffed his able lieutenants Ge Yang, Lu Xiu, Wei Yi, Liu Zhen, and Han Tai as county dukes, trusted them as his inner circle, and called them the "Five Dukes."

sentences.zh: 成都王穎至鄴，詔遣使者就申前命；

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying reached Ye; an edict sent envoys to confirm the previous appointment;
translations.idiomatic: When Ying reached Ye, the court sent envoys to confirm his earlier appointment;

sentences.zh: 穎受大將軍，讓九錫殊禮。

translations.literal: Sima Ying accepted Grand General and declined the Nine Bestowals and special rites.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted the post of Grand General but declined the Nine Bestowals and other extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 表論興義功臣，皆封公侯。

translations.literal: He memorialized discussing the merits of those who rose in righteousness, all enfeoffed as dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on behalf of the righteous coalition and had every meritorious commander enfeoffed as duke or marquis.

sentences.zh: 又表稱：「大司馬前在陽翟，與賊相持既久，百姓困敝，乞運河北邸閣米十五萬斛，以振陽翟饑民。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized saying: "The Grand Marshal earlier at Yangzhai was long locked with the rebels, and the common people were worn and exhausted; I beg to transport one hundred fifty thousand hu of grain from the Hebei government storehouses to relieve the starving people of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Grand Marshal Jiong, who had held Yangzhai for a long time while the people suffered, be allowed to ship one hundred fifty thousand hu of grain from the Hebei granaries to feed the hungry there.

sentences.zh: 造棺八千餘枚，以成都國秩為衣服，斂祭黃橋戰士，旌顯其家，加常戰亡二等。

translations.literal: He had eight thousand-plus coffins made, using Chengdu principality stipend for clothing, collecting and burying the Huangqiao warriors, honoring and displaying their families, raising by two ranks those who died in ordinary combat.
translations.idiomatic: He had more than eight thousand coffins made, paid for burial clothes from the Chengdu principality revenue, buried and honored the dead of Huangqiao, praised their families publicly, and raised the rank of ordinary war dead by two degrees.

sentences.zh: 又命溫縣瘞趙王倫戰士萬四千餘人。

translations.literal: He also ordered Wen county to bury more than fourteen thousand of the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun's warriors.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wen county to bury more than fourteen thousand of Lun's soldiers.

sentences.zh: 皆盧志之謀也。

translations.literal: All were Lu Zhi's plans.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was Lu Zhi's counsel.

sentences.zh: 穎形美而神昏，不知書，然氣性敦厚，委事於志，故得成其美焉。

translations.literal: Sima Ying's form was handsome but his spirit muddled; he did not know books, yet his temperament was honest and thick, and he entrusted affairs to Zhi—therefore he could accomplish his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was handsome but dull, illiterate yet good-natured. He left affairs to Lu Zhi, and so his virtues shone.

sentences.zh: 詔復遣使諭穎入輔，並使受九錫。

translations.literal: An edict again sent envoys to instruct Sima Ying to enter and assist, and also to accept the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent envoys urging Ying to return and assist the government and to accept the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 穎嬖人孟玖不欲還洛，又程太妃愛戀鄴都，故穎終辭不拜。

translations.literal: Sima Ying's favorite Meng Jiu did not wish to return to Luo, and also the Princess Dowager Cheng loved Ye—therefore Sima Ying in the end declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Meng Jiu did not want to go back to Luoyang, and Princess Dowager Cheng loved Ye, so Ying finally refused.

sentences.zh: 初，大司馬冏疑中書郎陸機為趙王倫撰禪詔，收，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Marshal Sima Jiong suspected Secretariat Lang Lu Ji had drafted the abdication edict for the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun, arrested him, and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand Marshal Jiong had suspected secretariat officer Lu Ji of drafting Lun's abdication edict for him. Ji was arrested and Jiong meant to execute him.

sentences.zh: 大將軍穎為之辯理，得免死，因表為平原內史，以其弟雲為清河內史。

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Ying pled on his behalf and he escaped death; thereby Sima Ying memorialized making him Interior Minister of Pingyuan, and his younger brother Yun Interior Minister of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Ying spoke for him and saved his life. Ying then had him appointed interior minister of Pingyuan and his brother Yun interior minister of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 機友人顧榮及廣陵戴淵，以中國多難，勸機還吳。

translations.literal: Ji's friend Gu Rong and Guangling's Dai Yuan, because China had many troubles, urged Ji to return to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His friends Gu Rong and Dai Yuan of Guangling, seeing turmoil across the central plains, urged Ji to go home to Wu.

sentences.zh: 機以受穎全濟之恩，且謂穎有時望，可與立功，遂留不去。

translations.literal: Ji because he had received Sima Ying's grace in being fully saved, and moreover considered Sima Ying had reputation for the times and could be joined in establishing achievement, thereupon stayed and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ji felt bound by Ying's kindness in sparing his life and believed Ying still had a future in which they might achieve something together, so he stayed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，復封常山王乂為長沙王，遷開府，驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, again enfeoffed Prince of Changshan Sima Yi as Prince of Changsha, transferred to open office, Cavalry General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Prince of Changshan, Sima Yi, was again enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha, given an open office, and appointed Cavalry General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 東萊王蕤，凶暴使酒，數陵侮大司馬冏，又從冏求開府不得而怨之，密表冏專權，與左衛將軍王輿謀廢冏。

translations.literal: Prince of Dailai Sima Rui was fierce and given to drink, repeatedly insulted Grand Marshal Sima Jiong, and because he asked Jiong for an open office without success resented him; he secretly memorialized that Jiong monopolized power, and with Left Guard General Wang Yu plotted to depose Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dailai, Sima Rui, was violent and drunken and repeatedly humiliated Grand Marshal Jiong. When Jiong refused his request for an open office, Rui turned against him. He secretly reported Jiong's monopoly of power and conspired with Left Guard General Wang Yu to remove him.

sentences.zh: 事覺，八月，詔廢蕤為庶人，誅輿三族，徒蕤於上庸；

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; in the eighth month an edict deposed Rui to commoner status, executed Yu and his clan to the third degree, and exiled Rui to Shangyong;
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, an edict in the eighth month reduced Rui to commoner rank, put Wang Yu's clan to death through the third degree of kinship, and banished Rui to Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 上庸內史陳鐘承冏旨潛殺之。

translations.literal: Shangyong Interior Minister Chen Zhong, carrying out Jiong's intent, secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhong, interior minister of Shangyong, carried out Jiong's orders and had him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 東武公澹坐不孝徙遼東。

translations.literal: Duke of Dongwu Dan was convicted of unfilial conduct and exiled to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, was found guilty of unfilial conduct and banished to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 九月，征其弟東安王繇復舊爵，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month his younger brother Prince of Dong'an Sima Yao was summoned and restored to his former rank, and appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month his younger brother, the Prince of Dong'an, Sima Yao, was recalled and restored to his former title and made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 繇舉東平王楙為平東將軍、都督徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。

translations.literal: Yao recommended Prince of Dongping Sima Mao as General Who Pacifies the East and Supervisor of all military affairs in Xuzhou, stationed at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao had the Prince of Dongping, Sima Mao, appointed General Who Pacifies the East and put in command of all military affairs in Xuzhou, with his headquarters at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷符下秦、雍州，使召還流民入蜀者，又遣御史馮該、張昌督之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court had issued orders to Qin and Yong provinces to summon back the migrant people who had entered Shu, and also sent censors Feng Gai and Zhang Chang to supervise the recall.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had ordered Qin and Yong provinces to recall the refugees who had gone into Shu, and sent censors Feng Gai and Zhang Chang to enforce it.

sentences.zh: 李特兄輔自略陽至蜀，言中國方亂，不足復還。

translations.literal: Li Te's elder brother Fu came from Lueyang to Shu and said the central lands were in turmoil and it was not worth returning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's elder brother Fu arrived in Shu from Lueyang and told him the heartland was in chaos and there was no point in going back.

sentences.zh: 特然之，累遣天水閻式詣羅尚求權停至秋，又納賂於尚及馮該；

translations.literal: Te agreed; he repeatedly sent Yan Shi of Tianshui to Luo Shang to ask permission to halt until autumn, and also offered bribes to Shang and Feng Gai;
translations.idiomatic: Te agreed. Again and again he sent Yan Shi of Tianshui to Luo Shang to plead for a stay until autumn, and he also bribed Shang and Feng Gai.

sentences.zh: 尚、該許之。

translations.literal: Shang and Gai consented.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Gai agreed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷論討趙廞功，拜特宣威將軍，弟流奮武將軍，皆封侯。

translations.literal: The court discussed rewards for merit in suppressing Zhao Yin; Te was appointed General Who Proclaims Might, his younger brother Liu General Who Stirs Martial Valor—both were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: When the court weighed merit in putting down Zhao Yin, Te was made General Who Proclaims Might and his brother Liu General Who Stirs Martial Valor; both received marquisates.

sentences.zh: 璽書下益州，條列六郡流民與特同討廞者，將加封賞。

translations.literal: An imperial letter went down to Yizhou listing the migrant people of the six commanderies who had joined Te in attacking Yin, to be given further titles and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript reached Yizhou with a roster of refugees from the six commanderies who had fought Yin alongside Te, promising them further honors and rewards.

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守辛冉欲以滅廞為己功，寢朝命，不以實上，眾咸怨之。

translations.literal: Guanghan Administrator Xin Ran wished to claim the credit for destroying Yin for himself; he suppressed the court's orders and did not report the facts upward, and the multitude all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran, administrator of Guanghan, wanted the glory of destroying Yin for himself. He sat on the court's orders and never reported what had really happened, and everyone grew bitter toward him.

sentences.zh: 羅尚遣從事督遣流民，限七月上道。

translations.literal: Luo Shang sent staff to supervise and drive off the migrants, setting a deadline of the seventh month for them to be on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang sent officials to press the refugees to leave, with orders to be on the road by the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 時流民布在梁、益，為人傭力，聞州郡逼遣，人人愁怨，不知所為；

translations.literal: At the time the migrants were scattered through Liang and Yi, working as hired labor; when they heard the provinces were forcing them away, every man was full of dread and did not know what to do;
translations.idiomatic: The refugees were spread across Liang and Yi, hiring themselves out for wages. When word came that the provinces were driving them out, dread spread through every camp and no one knew which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 且水潦方盛，年谷未登，無以為行資。

translations.literal: Moreover floods were still heavy, the year's grain not yet ripe, and there was nothing for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Floods were still raging, the harvest was not in, and they had nothing to live on for the journey.

sentences.zh: 特復遣閻式詣尚，求停至冬；

translations.literal: Te again sent Yan Shi to Shang to ask to halt until winter;
