translations.idiomatic: Te sent Yan Shi to Shang again to ask for a delay until winter.

sentences.zh: 辛冉及犍為太守苾以為不可。

translations.literal: Xin Ran and Jianwei Administrator Li Bi said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran and Li Bi, prefect of Jianwei, refused.

sentences.zh: 尚舉別駕蜀郡杜苾秀才，式為苾說逼移利害，苾亦欲寬流民一年；

translations.literal: Shang had nominated Registrar Du Bi of Shu commandery as a talent; Shi explained to Bi the harm in forced relocation, and Bi also wished to give the migrants one more year;
translations.idiomatic: Shang had named Du Bi of Shu commandery as his registrar. Shi laid out for Bi the damage a forced move would do, and Bi too wanted to give the refugees another year.

sentences.zh: 尚用冉、苾之謀，不從；

translations.literal: Shang followed the plans of Ran and Bi and did not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Shang took Ran and Bi's advice and would not budge.

sentences.zh: 苾乃致秀才板，出還家。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon returned his registrar's tablet and went home.
translations.idiomatic: Bi handed back his registrar's tablet and went home.

sentences.zh: 冉性貪暴，欲殺流民首領，取其資貨，乃與苾白尚，言：「流民前因趙廞之亂，多所剽掠，宜因移設關以奪取之。」

translations.literal: Ran was greedy and brutal and wished to kill migrant leaders and seize their goods; he and Bi told Shang, saying: "The migrants earlier, because of Zhao Yin's disorder, did much plundering—it is fitting, as they move, to set passes and seize their goods."
translations.idiomatic: Ran was greedy and cruel and wanted to kill refugee leaders and take their property. He and Bi told Shang, "During Zhao Yin's revolt these people looted far and wide. Use the move as a pretext—set checkpoints and strip them of what they carry."

sentences.zh: 尚移書令梓潼太守張演於諸要施關，搜索寶貨。

translations.literal: Shang sent a letter ordering Zitong Administrator Zhang Yan to set passes at key points and search out valuables.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ordered Zitong prefect Zhang Yan to set up barriers at the choke points and search out their valuables.

sentences.zh: 特數為流民請留，流民皆感而恃之，多相帥歸特。

translations.literal: Te repeatedly pleaded on the migrants' behalf to let them stay; the migrants were all moved and relied on him, and many took one another as leaders to join Te.
translations.idiomatic: Te kept petitioning for the refugees to remain, and they came to trust him. More and more bands chose him as their head.

sentences.zh: 特乃結大營於綿竹以處流民，移辛冉求自寬。

translations.literal: Te then built a great camp at Mianzhu to house the migrants, and sent word to Xin Ran asking for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Te pitched a great camp at Mianzhu for the refugees and asked Xin Ran to ease the pressure.

sentences.zh: 冉大怒，遣人分榜通衢，購募特兄弟，許以重賞。

translations.literal: Ran was furious and sent men to post notices along the main roads, offering a reward for the Te brothers, promising heavy payment.
translations.idiomatic: Ran flew into a rage and had notices posted on every highway, offering a rich price for the Te brothers' heads.

sentences.zh: 特見之，悉取以歸，與弟驤改其購云：「能送六郡之豪李、任、閻、趙、楊、上官及氐、叟侯王一首，賞百匹。」

translations.literal: When Te saw them he took them all back; with his brother Xiang he altered the offer to read: "Whoever delivers one head among the great families of the six commanderies—Li, Ren, Yan, Zhao, Yang, Shangguan—and among the Di and Sao tribal kings, shall receive one hundred bolts of cloth."
translations.idiomatic: Te collected the notices and, with his brother Xiang, rewrote them: "One hundred bolts of cloth for whoever brings in a head from the great houses of the six commanderies—Li, Ren, Yan, Zhao, Yang, Shangguan—or from the Di and Sao kings."

sentences.zh: 於是流民大懼，歸特者愈眾，旬月間過二萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the migrants were greatly afraid; those joining Te grew ever more numerous—in a little over a month more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The refugees were terrified. Still more flocked to Te, and in little more than a month his following passed twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 流亦聚眾數千人。

translations.literal: Liu also gathered a host of several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Liu mustered several thousand men of his own.

sentences.zh: 特又遣閻式詣羅尚求申期，式見營柵衝要，謀掩流民，歎曰：「民心方危，今而速之，亂將作矣。」

translations.literal: Te again sent Yan Shi to Luo Shang to ask for an extension; Shi saw camps and stockades blocking the passes and a plot to trap the migrants, and sighed: "The people's hearts are already shaken—hurry them now and revolt will follow."
translations.idiomatic: Te sent Yan Shi to Shang once more for more time. Shi saw stockades across the passes, meant to trap the refugees, and said, "Their hearts are already frayed. Push them now and you will have rebellion."

sentences.zh: 又知辛冉、李苾意不可回，乃辭尚還綿竹。

translations.literal: He also knew Xin Ran and Li Bi's minds could not be turned, and so took leave of Shang and returned to Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He saw that Ran and Li Bi would not bend, bade Shang farewell, and went back to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 尚謂式曰：「子且以吾意告諸流民，今聽寬矣。」

translations.literal: Shang said to Shi: "You may tell the migrants on my behalf that they are allowed a reprieve now."
translations.idiomatic: Shang told him, "Carry my word to the refugees—they may have more time."

sentences.zh: 式曰：「明公惑於奸說，恐無寬理。

translations.literal: Shi said: "My lord is misled by treacherous counsel; I fear there will be no reprieve.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "You are listening to traitors. I do not believe there will be any reprieve.

sentences.zh: 弱而不可輕者民也，今趣之不以理，眾怒難犯，恐為禍不淺。」

translations.literal: The weak must not be treated lightly—the people. Drive them now without justice and their anger will be hard to face; I fear the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: The people seem weak, but they must not be slighted. Hound them without right and their wrath will be impossible to hold back. The ruin may be deep."

sentences.zh: 尚曰：「然。

translations.literal: Shang said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Shang said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 吾不欺子，子其行矣！」

translations.literal: I will not deceive you—go!"
translations.idiomatic: I will not lie to you. Go."

sentences.zh: 式至綿竹，言於特曰：「尚雖云爾，然未可信也。

translations.literal: When Shi reached Mianzhu he said to Te: "Though Shang spoke thus, he is not yet to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At Mianzhu he told Te, "Shang spoke fairly, but you cannot trust him yet.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 尚威刑不立，冉等各擁強兵，一旦為變，亦非尚所能制，深宜為備。」

translations.literal: Shang's authority and punishments do not stand firm; Ran and the others each hold strong troops—if trouble breaks out in a day, Shang cannot control it either. You should prepare deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Shang cannot enforce his will. Ran and the rest command their own armies. If something snaps, Shang will not be able to stop it. Arm yourself now."

sentences.zh: 特從之。

translations.literal: Te followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Te took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，特分為二營，特居北營，流居東營，繕甲厲兵，戒嚴以待之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Te divided into two camps—Te in the north camp, Liu in the east camp—repairing armor and sharpening weapons, on alert and waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Te split his force into two camps: he took the north, Liu the east. They repaired armor, sharpened blades, and waited under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 冉、苾相與謀曰：「羅侯貪而無斷，日復一日，令流民得展奸計。

translations.literal: Ran and Bi plotted together, saying: "Lord Luo is greedy and indecisive; day after day he lets the migrants carry out their wicked schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Ran and Bi schemed together. "Luo is greedy and cannot decide. Day by day he lets the refugees plot.

sentences.zh: 李特兄弟並有雄才，吾屬將為所虜矣！

translations.literal: The Li Te brothers all have heroic talent—we are about to be made their captives!
translations.idiomatic: The Te brothers are born leaders. We are going to be their prisoners!

sentences.zh: 宜為決計，羅侯不足復問也！」

translations.literal: We ought to settle this decisively—Lord Luo is not worth consulting further!"
translations.idiomatic: We must act now. There is no point in asking Luo again."

sentences.zh: 乃遣廣漢都尉曾元、牙門張顯、劉並等潛帥步騎三萬襲特營；

translations.literal: They then sent Guanghan Commandant Zeng Yuan, Gate Officer Zhang Xian, Liu Bing, and others secretly to lead thirty thousand foot and horse in a surprise attack on Te's camp;
translations.idiomatic: They sent Guanghan commandant Zeng Yuan, gate officers Zhang Xian and Liu Bing, and others to steal upon Te's camp with thirty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 羅尚聞之，亦遣督護田佐助元。

translations.literal: When Luo Shang heard of it he also sent Supervisor Tian Zuo to assist Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang heard, he sent supervisor Tian Zuo to reinforce Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元等至，特安臥不動，待其眾半入，發伏擊之，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Yuan and the rest arrived, Te lay at ease without moving; when half their force had entered he sprang the ambush and struck—dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's men arrived to find Te seemingly asleep. When half the column was inside the camp, Te sprang his ambush. The dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 殺田佐、曾元、張顯，傳首以示尚、冉。

translations.literal: He killed Tian Zuo, Zeng Yuan, and Zhang Xian, and sent their heads to display before Shang and Ran.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Tian Zuo, Zeng Yuan, and Zhang Xian and sent their heads to Shang and Ran.

sentences.zh: 尚謂將佐曰：「此虜成去矣，而廣漢不用吾言以張賊勢，今若之何！」

translations.literal: Shang said to his officers: "These bandits are firmly gone now, yet Guanghan would not heed my words and has swollen the rebels' power—what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Shang told his staff, "The rebels are beyond recall, and Guanghan ignored me and fed their strength. What now?"

sentences.zh: 於是六郡流民李含等共推特行鎮北大將軍，承製封拜；

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Han of the six commanderies' migrants and others together urged Te to act as General Who Pacifies the North, with commissions and enfeoffments by imperial order on his own authority;
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Han and other refugee leaders from the six commanderies urged Te to take the title General Who Pacifies the North and issue his own commissions and enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 以其弟流行鎮東大將軍，號東督護，以相鎮統；

translations.literal: making his younger brother Liu General Who Pacifies the East, styled Eastern Supervisor, so the two might command in tandem;
translations.idiomatic: They made his brother Liu General Who Pacifies the East, Eastern Supervisor, so the two could command as one.

sentences.zh: 又以兄輔為驃騎將軍，弟驤為驍騎將軍，進兵攻冉於廣漢。

translations.literal: also making elder brother Fu Cavalry General-in-Chief and younger brother Xiang Valiant Cavalry General, and advancing to attack Ran in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Fu became Cavalry General-in-Chief and his younger brother Xiang Valiant Cavalry General, and they marched on Ran in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 尚遣李苾、費遠帥眾救冉，畏特，不敢進。

translations.literal: Shang sent Li Bi and Fei Yuan leading troops to rescue Ran, but they feared Te and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shang sent Li Bi and Fei Yuan to relieve Ran, but they were afraid of Te and would not move.

sentences.zh: 冉出戰，屢敗，潰圍奔德陽。

translations.literal: Ran came out to fight, was repeatedly defeated, broke through the encirclement and fled to Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ran fought and lost again and again, broke out of the ring, and fled to Deyang.

sentences.zh: 特入據廣漢，以李超為太守，進兵攻尚於成都。

translations.literal: Te entered and seized Guanghan, made Li Chao administrator, and advanced to attack Shang at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Te took Guanghan, installed Li Chao as administrator, and pressed Shang at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 尚以書諭閻式，式復書曰：「辛冉傾巧，曾元小豎，李叔平非將帥之材。

translations.literal: Shang sent a letter admonishing Yan Shi; Shi replied: "Xin Ran is cunning, Zeng Yuan a stripling, Li Shuping no material for a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shang wrote to admonish Yan Shi. Shi answered, "Xin Ran is sly, Zeng Yuan a boy, Li Shuping no soldier.

sentences.zh: 式前為節下及杜景文論留、徙之宜，人懷桑梓，孰不願之！

translations.literal: Earlier I argued before my lord and Du Jingwen on the right course for staying or moving—the people all cherish their native places; who would not wish to return!
translations.idiomatic: I pleaded with you and Du Jingwen to let them stay or go in due season. Every man longs for home. Who would not want to go back?

sentences.zh: 但往日初至，隨谷庸賃，一室五分，復值秋潦，乞須冬熟，而終不見聽。

translations.literal: But when they first arrived they hired themselves out by the grain, five parts to the house; then autumn floods came and they begged to wait until winter's ripening—and in the end no one would listen.
translations.idiomatic: When they came they worked for a pittance, five parts in ten to the landlord. Floods followed. They asked only to wait for the winter harvest. No one listened.

sentences.zh: 繩之太過，窮鹿抵虎。

translations.literal: The rope was drawn too tight—a cornered deer will butt a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: You pulled the rope too hard. A deer at bay will charge a tiger.

sentences.zh: 流民不肯延頸受刀，以致為變。

translations.literal: The migrants would not stretch their necks for the blade, and so trouble arose.
translations.idiomatic: They would not offer their necks to the knife. That is how this began.

sentences.zh: 即聽式言，寬使治嚴，不過去九月盡集，十月進道，令達鄉里，何有如此也！」

translations.literal: Had you only heeded my words, allowed them to prepare, no later than the end of the ninth month to gather, the tenth month to march—so they might reach their home villages—how could it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Had you taken my counsel—let them pack, gather by month's end in the ninth, march in the tenth, and reach their villages—how would we be here?"

sentences.zh: 特以兄輔、弟驤、子始、蕩、雄及李含、含子國、離、任回、李攀、攀弟恭、上官晶、任臧、楊褒、上官悖等為將帥，閻式、李遠等為僚佐。

translations.literal: Te made elder brother Fu, younger brothers Xiang, Shi, Dang, Xiong, and Li Han, Han's son Guo, Li, Ren Hui, Li Pan, Pan's younger brother Gong, Shangguan Jing, Ren Zang, Yang Bao, Shangguan Bei, and others his commanders, with Yan Shi, Li Yuan, and others as staff.
translations.idiomatic: Te appointed his kin and allies—Fu, Xiang, Shi, Dang, Xiong, Li Han and Han's son Guo, Li, Ren Hui, Li Pan and Pan's brother Gong, Shangguan Jing, Ren Zang, Yang Bao, Shangguan Bei—as generals, with Yan Shi and Li Yuan among his advisers.

sentences.zh: 羅尚素貪殘，為百姓患。

translations.literal: Luo Shang had always been greedy and cruel, a scourge to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang had long been greedy and brutal, a curse to the people.

sentences.zh: 特與蜀民約法三章，施捨振貸，禮賢拔滯，軍政肅然，蜀民大悅。

translations.literal: Te made a three-article compact with the people of Shu, gave alms and relief loans, honored the worthy and raised the blocked; military and civil affairs were orderly, and the people of Shu were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Te proclaimed a three-article law for Shu, gave alms and loans, honored talent and lifted the overlooked, and kept army and state in order. The people of Shu rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 尚頻為特所敗，乃阻長圍，緣郫水作營，連延七百里，與特相拒，求救於梁州及南夷校尉。

translations.literal: Shang was repeatedly defeated by Te; he then built a long encirclement, along the Pi River made camps stretching seven hundred li, to resist Te, and asked Liang Province and the Colonel of the Southern Yi for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shang lost battle after battle to Te, drew a long cordon, and for seven hundred li along the Pi River built camps to hold him off, while begging Liang Province and the southern tribes command for help.

sentences.zh: 十二月，穎昌康公何劭薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Duke Kang of Yingchang He Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Duke of Yingchang, He Shao, died.

sentences.zh: 封太司馬冏子冰為樂安王，英為濟陽王，超為淮南王。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Sima Jiong's son Bing was enfeoffed Prince of Le'an, Ying Prince of Jiyang, and Chao Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's sons Bing, Ying, and Chao were made princes of Le'an, Jiyang, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝中之上太安元年（

translations.literal: Middle section of Emperor Xiaohui, upper part, first year of Taian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohui, middle reign, upper section, first year of Taian (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元三零二年）

translations.literal: renxu, 302 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renxu, 302 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，沖太孫尚薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, Heir Apparent Chong Sima Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, heir apparent Chong, Sima Shang, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙酉，梁孝王肜薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yiyou, Prince Xiao of Liang Sima Bian died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fifth month's yiyou day, the Prince of Liang, Sima Bian, died.

sentences.zh: 以右光祿大夫劉寔為太傅；

translations.literal: Right Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shi was appointed Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, Right Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 尋以老病罷。

translations.literal: Soon after, because of age and illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was removed on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒遣督護衙博討李特，軍於梓潼；

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong sent Supervisor Ya Bo to attack Li Te; the army camped at Zitong;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, sent supervisor Ya Bo against Li Te, encamping at Zitong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷復以張微為廣漢太守，軍於德陽；

translations.literal: the court again appointed Zhang Wei Guanghan Administrator; his army camped at Deyang;
translations.idiomatic: The court again named Zhang Wei administrator of Guanghan, with his force at Deyang.

sentences.zh: 羅尚遣督護張龜軍於繁城。

translations.literal: Luo Shang sent Supervisor Zhang Gui with an army at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang sent supervisor Zhang Gui to camp at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 特使其子鎮軍將軍蕩等襲博；

translations.literal: Te sent his son General Who Stabilizes the Army Dang and others to strike Bo;
translations.idiomatic: Te sent his son Dang, General Who Stabilizes the Army, against Bo.

sentences.zh: 而自將擊龜，破之。

translations.literal: he himself led the attack on Gui and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He led the main force against Gui and broke him.

sentences.zh: 蕩敗博兵於陽沔，梓潼太守張演委城走，巴西丞毛植以郡降。

translations.literal: Dang defeated Bo's army at Yangmian; Zitong Administrator Zhang Yan abandoned the city and fled, and Brazilian Assistant Mao Zhi surrendered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangmian, Dang routed Bo. Zhang Yan, prefect of Zitong, fled an empty city, and Mao Zhi, assistant in Brazilian commandery, surrendered his province.

sentences.zh: 蕩進攻博於葭萌，博走，其眾盡降。

translations.literal: Dang pressed the attack on Bo at Jiameng; Bo fled and his entire force surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dang drove Bo from Jiameng. Bo ran, and his whole army came over.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒更以許雄為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong replaced him with Xu Xiong as Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong replaced Bo with Xu Xiong as inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 特自稱大將軍、益州牧，都督梁、益二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Te styled himself Grand General, Governor of Yizhou, and Supervisor of all military affairs in Liang and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Te took the titles Grand General, Governor of Yizhou, and commander of all forces in Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 大司馬冏欲久專大政，以帝子孫俱盡，大將軍穎有次立之勢；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Sima Jiong wished to monopolize government for long; because the emperor's sons and grandsons were all gone, Grand General Sima Ying had the momentum of the next succession;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Jiong meant to rule alone for good. With the emperor's sons and grandsons dead, Grand General Ying stood next in line for the throne.

sentences.zh: 清河王覃，遐之子也，方八歲，乃上表請立之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Sima Tan, son of Sima Xia, was only eight years old; Jiong therefore memorialized asking that he be established.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe, Sima Tan, Xia's son, was only eight. Jiong memorialized to make him heir.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，立覃為皇太子，以冏為太子太師，東海王越為司空，領中書監。

translations.literal: On guimao Tan was established as crown prince; Jiong was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Prince of Donghai Sima Yue Director of Works overseeing the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Tan was named crown prince. Jiong became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, Director of Works with charge of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，李特攻張微，微擊破之，遂進攻特營。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Li Te attacked Zhang Wei; Wei struck and defeated him, then advanced to attack Te's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Li Te attacked Zhang Wei. Wei beat him back and pressed on to Te's camp.

sentences.zh: 李蕩引兵救之，山道險狹，蕩力戰而前，遂破微兵。

translations.literal: Li Dang led troops to the rescue; the mountain road was narrow and steep, Dang fought his way forward with force, and so broke Wei's army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang came up to help. The pass was tight; he fought forward foot by foot and shattered Wei's line.

sentences.zh: 特欲還涪，蕩及司馬王幸諫曰：「微軍已敗，智勇俱竭，宜乘銳氣遂禽之。」

translations.literal: Te wished to return to Fu; Dang and Marshal Wang Xing remonstrated: "Wei's army is already defeated, his wit and courage both spent—you ought to ride this sharp momentum and take him."
translations.idiomatic: Te meant to pull back to Fu. Dang and marshal Wang Xing urged him on: "Wei is broken—mind and nerve spent. Press the advantage and take him."

sentences.zh: 特復進攻微，殺之，生禽微子存，以微喪還之。

translations.literal: Te again advanced to attack Wei, killed him, captured alive Wei's son Cun, and returned Wei's coffin to him.
translations.idiomatic: Te attacked again, killed Wei, took his son Cun alive, and sent Wei's body home.

sentences.zh: 特以其將寋碩守德陽。

translations.literal: Te made his general Ning Shuo hold Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: He left his general Ning Shuo to hold Deyang.

sentences.zh: 李驤軍毘橋，羅尚遣軍擊之，屢為驤所敗，驤遂進攻成都，燒其門。

translations.literal: Li Xiang's army was at Piqiao; Luo Shang sent troops to strike him, was repeatedly defeated by Xiang, and Xiang then advanced to attack Chengdu and burned its gates.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang camped at Piqiao. Shang sent troops against him, lost again and again, and Xiang pushed on to Chengdu and set fire to its gates.

sentences.zh: 李流軍成都之北，尚遣精勇萬人攻驤，驤與流合擊，大破之，還者什一二。

translations.literal: Li Liu's army was north of Chengdu; Shang sent ten thousand picked men to attack Xiang; Xiang and Liu joined forces and struck a great defeat—of those who returned, only one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu held the north of the city. Shang sent ten thousand elites against Xiang. Xiang and Liu struck together and broke them—barely one in ten came back.

sentences.zh: 許雄數遣軍攻特，不勝，特勢益盛。

translations.literal: Xu Xiong repeatedly sent armies to attack Te without success; Te's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiong attacked Te again and again without winning, and Te's power only swelled.

sentences.zh: 建寧大姓李睿、毛詵逐太守杜俊，朱提大姓李猛逐太守雍約，以應特，眾各數萬。

translations.literal: Great clans of Jianning—Li Rui and Mao Shen—drove out Administrator Du Jun; great clans of Zhuti—Li Meng—drove out Administrator Yong Yue, all in response to Te, each host numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianning the great houses Li Rui and Mao Shen drove out prefect Du Jun; in Zhuti Li Meng drove out Yong Yue—each rising for Te with tens of thousands behind him.

sentences.zh: 南夷校尉李毅討破之，斬詵；

translations.literal: Colonel of the Southern Yi Li Yi attacked and defeated them, beheading Shen;
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Southern Yi Li Yi crushed them and beheaded Shen.

sentences.zh: 李猛奉箋降，而辭意不遜，毅誘而殺之。

translations.literal: Li Meng submitted a letter of surrender, but the wording was not submissive; Yi lured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Meng sent a letter of submission, insolent in tone. Yi enticed him in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丙戌，復置寧州，以毅為刺史。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, Ning Province was re-established; Yi was made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, Ning Province was restored and Li Yi was appointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 齊武閔王冏既得志，頗驕奢擅權，大起府第，壞公私廬舍以百數，制與西宮等，中外失望。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi and Wu Min, Sima Jiong, having attained his aim, grew quite arrogant and extravagant and monopolized power; he raised great mansions for his residence, destroyed public and private buildings by the hundreds, and made his establishment equal to the Western Palace; inside and outside the court were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi and Duke of Wu Min, had his victory, he turned arrogant and grasping. He threw up palaces by the hundred, tore down public and private houses alike, and built to match the Western Palace. Court and country lost heart.

sentences.zh: 侍中嵇紹上疏曰：「存不忘亡，《易》之善戒也。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Shao submitted a memorial, saying: "To preserve and not forget perishing is the fine admonition of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao, attendant-in-ordinary, wrote in: "The Changes teach a good warning: hold fast to life, but never forget how easily it is lost.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下無忘金墉，大司馬無忘穎上，大將軍無忘黃橋，則禍亂之萌無由而兆矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty not to forget Jinyong, the Grand Marshal not to forget Ying, the Great General not to forget Huangqiao—then the sprouts of disaster and disorder will have no means to appear.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remember Jinyong, the Grand Marshal to remember Ying, the Great General to remember Huangqiao—then the first stirrings of ruin will never find a foothold.

sentences.zh: 又與冏書，以為「唐、虞茅茨，夏禹卑宮。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Jiong, saying that "Tang and Yu had thatched roofs; Yu of Xia had a humble palace.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Jiong as well: "Tang and Yu lived under thatch; Yu of Xia kept his halls low.

sentences.zh: 今大興第捨，及為三王立宅，豈今日之所急邪！」

translations.literal: Now you greatly raise residences and build houses for the three princes—is this what today urgently needs!"
translations.idiomatic: You are raising mansions on every side and building homes for three princes. Is that what the realm needs now?"

sentences.zh: 冏遜辭謝之，然不能從。

translations.literal: Jiong declined with apologies, yet could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong answered with thanks and apology, but he would not change course.

sentences.zh: 冏耽於宴樂，不入朝見；

translations.literal: Jiong indulged in feasting and music and did not enter court for audience;
translations.idiomatic: Jiong drowned himself in feasts and song and stopped coming to court;

sentences.zh: 坐拜百官，符敕三台；

translations.literal: seated, received the obeisance of all officials; issued tokens and edicts to the Three Platforms;
translations.idiomatic: he sat while officials bowed to him and sent orders straight to the Three Platforms;

sentences.zh: 選舉不均，嬖寵用事。

translations.literal: appointments were uneven; favorites held affairs.
translations.idiomatic: promotions were rigged and pet lovers ran the government.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史桓豹奏事，不先經冏府，即加考竟。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Huan Bao presented affairs without first passing through Jiong's office; he was immediately subjected to examination unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Huan Bao reported a matter without routing it through Jiong's office. Jiong had him interrogated to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 南陽處士鄭方上書諫冏曰：「今大王安不慮危，燕樂過度，一失也；

translations.literal: Recluse of Nanyang Zheng Fang submitted a letter remonstrating with Jiong, saying: "Now the Great King, secure, does not consider danger; feasting and pleasure in excess—that is one lapse;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Fang of Nanyang, a recluse, sent Jiong a remonstrance: "You rest easy and never think of peril, yet feast beyond measure—that is your first fault;

sentences.zh: 宗室骨肉，當無纖介，今則不然，二失也；

translations.literal: kinsmen of the imperial clan should be without the slightest alienation; now it is not so—two lapses;
translations.idiomatic: clan kin should stand without a hair's breadth between them, yet now they do not—your second fault;

sentences.zh: 蠻夷不靜，大王謂功業已隆，不以為念，三失也；

translations.literal: the barbarians are not quiet; the Great King thinks his merit and enterprise already lofty and does not take thought of it—three lapses;
translations.idiomatic: the frontier is unsettled, yet you treat your work as done and look away—that is the third;

sentences.zh: 兵革之後，百姓窮困，不聞振救，四失也；

translations.literal: after arms and armor, the people are destitute and hard pressed; one does not hear of relief and rescue—four lapses;
translations.idiomatic: after war the people are broken, and no relief reaches them—the fourth;

sentences.zh: 大王與義兵盟約，事定之後，賞不□俞時，而今猶有功未論者，五失也。」

translations.literal: the Great King made covenant with the righteous army; after affairs were settled, rewards were not timely, and even now there are still meritorious deeds not reckoned—five lapses."
translations.idiomatic: you swore rewards to the righteous armies, yet when the fighting ended payment lagged, and merit still goes unreckoned—that is the fifth."

sentences.zh: 冏謝曰：「非子，孤不聞過。」

translations.literal: Jiong apologized: "Without you, I would not have heard my faults."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong replied, "But for you, I would never have heard my faults."

sentences.zh: 孫惠上書曰：「天下有五難、四不可，而明公皆居之。

translations.literal: Sun Hui submitted a letter, saying: "Under Heaven there are five difficulties and four impossibilities, and the Illustrious Duke occupies them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui wrote in: "The world knows five hardships and four things that cannot last, and you, my lord, stand in every one of them.

sentences.zh: 冒犯鋒刃，一難也；

translations.literal: to brave the edge of blades—one difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: To face naked steel—that is the first hardship;

sentences.zh: 聚致英豪，二難也；

translations.literal: to gather and draw heroes—two difficulties;
translations.idiomatic: to rally heroes to your banner—the second;

sentences.zh: 與將士均勞苦，三難也；

translations.literal: to share hardship with officers and soldiers—three difficulties;
translations.idiomatic: to share camp and march with your men—the third;

sentences.zh: 以弱勝強，四難也；

translations.literal: to overcome the strong with the weak—four difficulties;
translations.idiomatic: to beat the strong with the weak—the fourth;

sentences.zh: 興復皇業，五難也。

translations.literal: to restore the imperial enterprise—five difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: to raise the house of Jin again—the fifth.

sentences.zh: 大名不可久荷，大功不可久任，大權不可久執，大威不可久居。

translations.literal: A great name cannot long be borne, great merit cannot long be held, great power cannot long be wielded, great awe cannot long be occupied.
translations.idiomatic: Great fame cannot be carried forever, nor great merit held, nor great power wielded, nor great dread kept.

sentences.zh: 大王行其難而不以為難，處其不可而謂之可，惠竊所不安也。

translations.literal: The Great King performs the difficult and does not regard it as difficult, dwells in the impossible and calls it possible—this is what Hui privately finds unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: You do what others call impossible and treat it as ordinary. That, my lord, is what unsettles me.

sentences.zh: 明公宜思功成身退之道。

translations.literal: The Illustrious Duke ought to consider the way of achieving the work and retiring the person.
translations.idiomatic: Think, my lord, of finishing the task and leaving the stage.

sentences.zh: 崇親推近，委重長沙、成都二王，長揖掃籓，則太伯，子臧不專美於前矣。

translations.literal: Honor the near kin and elevate those close, entrust weight to the two princes of Changsha and Chengdu, bow and sweep the frontier—then Grand Duke and Prince Zang would not monopolize praise before you.
translations.idiomatic: Elevate your kin, lean on the princes of Changsha and Chengdu, bow out to guard the realm, and you will match the Grand Duke and Prince Zang without letting them alone wear the glory.

sentences.zh: 今乃忘高亢之可危，貪權勢以受疑，雖遨遊高台之上，逍遙重墉之內，愚竊謂危亡之憂，過於在穎、翟之時也。」

translations.literal: Now you forget that lofty height can be perilous, and greedily hold power and position to incur suspicion; though you roam atop high towers and wander within layered walls, I privately think the worry of peril and ruin exceeds that of your days at Ying and Di."
translations.idiomatic: You forget that the higher you stand the harder the fall, and clutch office until men doubt you. You may stroll your high halls and thick walls, yet I believe you are in graver danger than at Ying or Di.

sentences.zh: 冏不能用。

translations.literal: Jiong could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong would not take his counsel.

sentences.zh: 惠辭疾去。

translations.literal: Hui pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui pleaded illness and left.

sentences.zh: 冏謂曹攄曰：「或勸吾委權還國，何如？」

translations.literal: Jiong said to Cao Shu: "Some urge me to relinquish power and return to my state—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong asked Cao Shu, "Some tell me to hand back power and go home to my fief. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 攄曰：「物禁太盛，大王誠能居高慮危，褰裳去之，斯善之善者也。

translations.literal: Shu said: "When things reach utmost fullness they are checked; if the Great King can truly dwell on high and consider peril, lift your robe and go—that would be the best of the good.
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered, "When a thing peaks it must break. If you can live high yet think low, gather your skirts and walk away—that is the best of goods.

sentences.zh: 冏不聽。

translations.literal: Jiong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 張翰、顧榮皆慮及禍，翰因秋風起，思菰榮、蓴羹、鱸魚鱠，歎曰：「人生貴適志耳，富貴何為！」

translations.literal: Zhang Han and Gu Rong both feared coming disaster; as the autumn wind rose, Han thought of wild rice, water-shield soup, and sliced perch, and sighed: "In life what is precious is to suit one's will—what is wealth and rank for!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han and Gu Rong both feared ruin. When the autumn wind rose, Han longed for home cooking—wild rice, water-shield broth, sliced perch—and sighed, "Life is about following your heart. What is rank for?"

sentences.zh: 即引去。

translations.literal: He immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 榮故酣飲，不省府事，長史葛旟以其廢職，白冏徙榮為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Rong deliberately drank deep and ignored office affairs; Chief Clerk Ge Yi reported his neglect of duty to Jiong, who moved Rong to be Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rong drank on and ignored the office. Chief clerk Ge Yi reported his neglect, and Jiong shifted him to attendant of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 穎川處士庾袞聞冏期年不朝，歎曰：「晉室卑矣，禍亂將興！」

translations.literal: Recluse of Yingchuan Yu Gun, hearing that Jiong had gone a full year without attending court, sighed: "The house of Jin is low indeed—disaster and disorder will arise!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gun of Yingchuan, a recluse, heard that Jiong had not come to court in a year and said, "Jin is sinking. Trouble is coming."

sentences.zh: 帥妻子逃於林慮山中。

translations.literal: He led wife and children and fled to the mountains of Linlu.
translations.idiomatic: He took his family and fled into the Linlu hills.

sentences.zh: 王豹致箋於冏曰：「伏思元康已來，宰相在位，未有一人獲終者，乃事勢使然，非皆為不善也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao sent a note to Jiong, saying: "Reflecting from the Yuankang era onward, of those who served as chief minister while in office, not one obtained a natural end—it was the force of affairs, not that all were unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao wrote Jiong: "Since Yuankang, no chief minister has died in office of old age. That is the way power works, not proof that every man was wicked.

sentences.zh: 今公克平禍亂，安國定家，乃復尋覆車之軌，欲冀長存，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now you have overcome disaster and disorder and settled state and family, yet again follow the track of overturned carts and hope for long survival—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: You ended the turmoil and steadied the realm, yet you tread the same rut as the men who fell before you and still hope to last. How can that be easy?

sentences.zh: 今河間樹根於關右，成都盤桓於舊魏，新野大封於江、漢，三王各以方剛強盛之年，並典戎馬，處要害之地，而明公以難賞之功，挾震主之威，獨據京都，專執大權，進則亢龍有悔，退則據於蒺藜，冀此求安，未見其福也。」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Hejian has roots in the Guanxi region, Chengdu lingers in old Wei territory, and Xinye has great enfeoffment in the Jiang and Han; the three princes, each in the vigor of youth and strength, all command war horses and stand in strategic places, while the Illustrious Duke, with hard-to-reward merit, holds awe that shakes the ruler, alone occupies the capital, and monopolizes great power—advance and the "arrogant dragon" has regret; retreat and you stand on thistles. To seek safety this way—I do not see its blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Hejian is rooted in the west, Chengdu holds old Wei, Xinye is planted on the Jiang and Han. Three young princes command armies on the choke points, while you, my lord, with unrewarded merit and a presence that shadows the throne, hold Luoyang alone. Advance, and you face the dragon's pride; retreat, and you stand on thorns. I see no safety in this path.

sentences.zh: 因請悉遣王侯之國，依周、召之法，以成都王為北州伯，治鄴；

translations.literal: He therefore asked that all princes be sent to their states, following the method of the Zhou dukes of Zhou and Shao, making the Prince of Chengdu northern regional lord with seat at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: He urged Jiong to send every prince to his fief, as in the days of the Zhou regents, making the Prince of Chengdu northern regional lord at Ye;

sentences.zh: 冏自為南州伯，治宛；

translations.literal: Jiong himself would be southern regional lord with seat at Wan;
translations.idiomatic: Jiong himself would be southern regional lord at Wan;

sentences.zh: 分河為界，各統王侯，以夾輔天子。

translations.literal: the Yellow River would be the boundary, each commanding princes to flank and support the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: the Yellow River would divide their realms, and each would flank the Son of Heaven with armed kin.

sentences.zh: 冏優令答之。

translations.literal: Jiong gave a gracious written reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong answered with a polite letter and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 長沙王冏見豹箋，謂冏曰：「小子離間骨肉，何不銅馳下打殺！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha, on seeing Bao's memorial, said to Jiong: "This boy drives wedges between flesh and bone—why not have him beaten to death beneath the bronze camels!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changsha read Bao's note and told Jiong, "This boy sows discord in the clan. Why not beat him to death under the bronze camels?"

sentences.zh: 冏乃奏豹讒內間外，坐生猜嫌，不忠不義，鞭殺之。

translations.literal: Jiong then memorialized that Bao slandered within and alienated without, thereby breeding suspicion, unfaithful and unrighteous, and had him flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong accused Bao of slandering kin and splitting the court, then had him flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 豹將死，曰：「縣吾頭大司馬門，見兵之攻齊也！」

translations.literal: As Bao was about to die, he said: "Hang my head at the Grand Marshal's gate and you will see the armies attack Qi!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao cried at the block, "Hang my head on the Grand Marshal's gate and you will see troops come against Qi!"

sentences.zh: 冏以河間王顒本附趙王倫，心常恨之。

translations.literal: Jiong, because the Prince of Hejian Yong had originally attached himself to Prince of Zhao Lun, constantly bore resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong still resented Yong of Hejian for having sided with Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史安定皇甫商，與顒長史李含不平。

translations.literal: Huangfu Shang of Anding, Governor of Liang Province, was on bad terms with Yong's chief clerk Li Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shang of Anding, governor of Liang, feuded with Yong's chief clerk Li Han.

sentences.zh: 含被征為翊軍校尉，時商參冏軍事，夏侯奭兄亦在冏府。

translations.literal: Han was summoned to be Colonel of the Guard Army; at the time Shang was assisting Jiong in military affairs, and the elder brother of Xiahou Shang was also in Jiong's office.
translations.idiomatic: Han was called up as colonel of the guard army. Shang was then on Jiong's staff, and an elder brother of the Xiahou clan served in Jiong's office as well.

sentences.zh: 含心不自安，又與冏右司馬趙驤有隙，遂單馬奔顒，詐稱受密詔，使顒誅冏，因說顒曰：「成都王至親，有大功，推讓還籓，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: Han felt ill at ease in his mind; he also had a rift with Jiong's Right Chief of Staff Zhao Xiang, and so rode alone to flee to Yong, falsely claiming he had received a secret edict for Yong to execute Jiong, and thereby urged Yong, saying: "The Prince of Chengdu is closest kin, with great merit; he yielded and returned to his frontier and has won the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in Luoyang and at odds with Jiong's right chief of staff Zhao Xiang, Han fled alone to Yong, claiming a secret order to kill Jiong. He told Yong, "The Prince of Chengdu is close kin with great merit. He gave up power and went home, and the realm loves him for it.

sentences.zh: 齊王越親而專政，朝廷側目。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi is more distant kin yet monopolizes government; the court looks askance.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi is more distant yet rules alone, and the court watches with narrowed eyes.

sentences.zh: 今檄長沙王使討齊，齊王必誅長沙，吾因以為齊罪而討之，必可禽也。

translations.literal: Now summon the Prince of Changsha to attack Qi; the Prince of Qi is sure to execute Changsha, and I will then take Qi's crime as cause to attack him—he can surely be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Summon the Prince of Changsha against Qi. Qi will kill Changsha, and we can march on Qi as the man who murdered kin. He will fall.

sentences.zh: 去齊立成都，除逼建親，以安社稷，大勳也。」

translations.literal: Remove Qi and establish Chengdu, eliminate compulsion and build closeness, to settle the altars of state—great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Topple Qi, raise Chengdu, ease coercion and knit the clan, and steady the altars. That would be a great deed.

sentences.zh: 顒從之。

translations.literal: Yong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong agreed.

sentences.zh: 是時，武帝族弟范陽王虓都督豫州諸軍事。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor's clansman, the Prince of Fanyang Chao, was Director of all military affairs of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Fanyang, Sima Chao, a clansman of Emperor Wu, directed all military affairs of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 顒上表陳冏罪狀，且言：「勒兵十萬，欲與成都王穎、新野王歆、范陽王虓共合洛陽，請長沙王乂廢冏還第，以穎代冏輔政。」

translations.literal: Yong submitted a memorial stating Jiong's crimes, and also said: "I am mustering a hundred thousand troops and wish to join with the Prince of Chengdu Ying, the Prince of Xinye Xin, and the Prince of Fanyang Chao to converge on Luoyang; I ask the Prince of Changsha Yi to depose Jiong and return him to his residence, and let Ying replace Jiong in assisting government."
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent up a bill of Jiong's crimes and wrote that he was raising a hundred thousand men to join Chengdu, Xinye, and Fanyang at Luoyang, asking Changsha to depose Jiong and send him home while Ying took the regency.

sentences.zh: 顒遂舉兵，以李含為都督，帥張方等趨洛陽，復遣使邀穎，穎將應之，盧志諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Yong then raised troops, making Li Han commander, leading Zhang Fang and others toward Luoyang; he again sent envoys to invite Ying—Ying was about to respond, but Lu Zhi remonstrated and he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched, put Li Han in command, and led Zhang Fang toward Luoyang. He invited Ying again. Ying meant to answer, but Lu Zhi warned him off and he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁卯，顒表至。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingmao, Yong's memorial arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day dingmao, Yong's memorial reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 冏大懼，會百官議之，曰：「孤首唱義兵，臣子之節，信著神明。

translations.literal: Jiong was greatly afraid and convened the hundred officials to discuss it, saying: "I was first to raise the righteous army—the minister's duty, faith manifest to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was terrified and called the officials in. He said, "I was first to raise the righteous armies. A subject's duty, plain to heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 今二王信讒作難，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Now the two princes trust slander and make trouble—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now two princes heed lies and rise against me. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 尚書令王戎曰：「公勳業誠大，然賞不及勞，故人懷貳心。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Rong said: "Your merit and enterprise are indeed great, yet rewards have not matched labor, so men harbor divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, minister of works, said, "Your deeds are great, but rewards lagged behind labor, so hearts are divided.

sentences.zh: 今二王兵盛，不可當也。

translations.literal: Now the two princes' armies are strong and cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies are strong. You cannot face them.

sentences.zh: 若以王就第，委權崇讓，庶可求安。」

translations.literal: If you go to your residence as prince, relinquish power and exalt yielding, perhaps you may seek safety."
translations.idiomatic: Go to your fief, yield power, bow low, and you may buy peace."

sentences.zh: 冏從事中郎葛旟怒曰：「三台納言，不恤王事。

translations.literal: Jiong's Attendant Gentleman Ge Yi angrily said: "The Three Platforms receive words yet do not care for the prince's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Yi, Jiong's attendant gentleman, blazed back: "The Three Platforms speak up yet spare no thought for the prince's house.

sentences.zh: 賞報稽緩，責不在府。

translations.literal: Rewards and requital are slow—the fault is not in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Slow pay is not this office's fault.

sentences.zh: 讒言逆亂，當其誅討，奈何虛承偽書，遽令公就第乎！

translations.literal: Slander and rebellion ought to be punished and attacked—why empty accept a forged letter and hastily order the prince to his residence!
translations.idiomatic: These are forged charges and open revolt. Punish them. Why swallow a fake letter and tell the prince to go home?

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，王侯就第，寧有得保妻子者邪？

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei, when princes and marquises went to their residences, was there ever one who kept wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, has any prince who went to his fief kept his wife and children alive?

sentences.zh: 議者可斬！」

translations.literal: Those who counsel thus may be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever says that may be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 百官震悚失色，戎偽藥發墮廁，得免。

translations.literal: The hundred officials trembled in fear and turned pale; Rong feigned a fit of medicine and fell into the privy, and so escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The hall went white with fear. Rong faked a fit, fell into a latrine, and lived.

sentences.zh: 李含屯陰盤，張方帥兵二萬軍新安，檄長沙王乂使討冏。

translations.literal: Li Han encamped at Yinpan; Zhang Fang led twenty thousand troops to garrison at Xin'an and issued a summons to the Prince of Changsha Yi to attack Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han camped at Yinpan. Zhang Fang took twenty thousand men to Xin'an and called on Changsha to attack Jiong.

sentences.zh: 冏遣董艾襲乂，乂將左右百餘人馳入宮，閉諸門，奉天子攻大司馬府，董艾陳兵宮西，縱火燒千秋神武門。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Dong Ai to strike Yi; Yi led a little more than a hundred men on the left and right in a dash into the palace, closed all gates, upheld the Son of Heaven and attacked the Grand Marshal's residence; Dong Ai arrayed troops west of the palace and set fire to the Qianqiu and Shenwu gates.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent Dong Ai against him. Yi raced into the palace with a little over a hundred guards, shut the gates, put the emperor at his back, and stormed the Grand Marshal's house. Dong Ai lined up west of the palace and burned the Qianqiu and Shenwu gates.

sentences.zh: 冏使人執騶虞幡唱云：「長沙王矯詔。」

translations.literal: Jiong had men seize the zouyu banner and proclaim: "The Prince of Changsha has forged an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's men raised the zouyu banner and cried that Changsha had forged an edict.

sentences.zh: 乂又稱「大司馬謀反」。

translations.literal: Yi in turn declared "the Grand Marshal plots rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered that the Grand Marshal was in revolt.

sentences.zh: 是夕，城內大戰，飛矢雨集，火光屬天。

translations.literal: That night, great battle within the city; flying arrows fell like rain; firelight linked to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That night the city became a battlefield. Arrows fell like rain and flames licked the sky.

sentences.zh: 帝幸上東門，矢集御前，群臣死者相枕。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the Upper East Gate; arrows clustered before the imperial presence; among the ministers the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached the Upper East Gate. Arrows clustered at his feet. Ministers died in heaps.

sentences.zh: 連戰三日，冏眾大敗，大司馬長史趙淵殺何勖，因執冏以降。

translations.literal: After three days of continuous fighting, Jiong's host was greatly defeated; Grand Marshal Chief Clerk Zhao Yuan killed He Xun and thereby seized Jiong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Three days of fighting broke Jiong's host. His chief clerk Zhao Yuan killed He Xun and seized Jiong.

sentences.zh: 冏至殿前，帝惻然，欲活之。

translations.literal: When Jiong reached the front of the hall, the emperor was moved and wished to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was brought before the throne. The emperor pitied him and wished to spare him.

sentences.zh: 乂叱左右趣牽出，斬於閶闔門外，徇首六軍，同黨皆夷三族，死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Yi shouted at those at hand to hurry and drag him out; he was beheaded outside the Changhe Gate, his head displayed before the six armies; all partisans were exterminated to the third degree; the dead numbered more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered his guards to drag Jiong out and cut off his head at the Changhe Gate. The head was shown to the six armies. Partisans were wiped out to the third degree. More than two thousand died.

sentences.zh: 囚冏子超、冰、英於金墉城，廢冏弟北海王寔。

translations.literal: Jiong's sons Chao, Bing, and Ying were imprisoned in Jinyong city; Jiong's younger brother the Prince of Beihai Shi was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's sons Chao, Bing, and Ying were shut in Jinyong. His brother, the Prince of Beihai, was deposed.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: There was an amnesty for all under Heaven and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was pardoned and the reign era changed.

sentences.zh: 李含等聞冏死，引兵還長安。

translations.literal: Li Han and the others, hearing Jiong was dead, led troops back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han and the rest, hearing Jiong was dead, marched back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂雖在朝廷，事無鉅細，皆就鄴諮大將軍穎。

translations.literal: Although the Prince of Changsha Yi was at court, in affairs great or small he all went to Ye to consult the Great General Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Though Changsha held court, every matter, great or small, was carried to Ye for Ying's word.

sentences.zh: 穎以孫惠為參軍，陸雲為右司馬。

translations.literal: Ying made Sun Hui his aide and Lu Yun his Right Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Ying made Sun Hui his aide and Lu Yun his right chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 是歲，陳留王薨，謚日魏元皇帝。

translations.literal: This year the Prince of Chenliu died; his posthumous title was Emperor Yuan of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Prince of Chenliu died and was posthumously titled Emperor Yuan of Wei.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑宇文單于莫圭部眾強盛，遣其弟屈雲攻慕容廆，廆擊其別帥素怒延，破之。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Wenyuan chieftain Mo Gui's following was strong and flourishing; he sent his younger brother Quyun to attack Murong Hui; Hui struck his detached commander Sunuyan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chieftain Mo Gui of the Wenyuan tribe was strong. He sent his brother Quyun against Murong Hui. Hui struck Quyun's detached commander Sunuyan and broke him.

sentences.zh: 素怒延恥之，復發兵十萬，圍廆於棘城。

translations.literal: Sunuyan, shamed, again raised a hundred thousand troops and besieged Hui at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shamed, Sunuyan raised a hundred thousand men and besieged Hui at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 廆眾皆懼，廆曰：「素怒延兵雖多而無法制，已在吾算中矣，諸君但為力戰，無所憂也！」

translations.literal: Hui's multitude were all afraid; Hui said: "Though Sunuyan's soldiers are many, they lack rules and methods; they are already within my reckoning—everyone only fight with force, and have no worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui's men were afraid. Hui said, "Sunuyan's horde is huge but lawless. I have already reckoned him out. Fight hard and do not fear."

sentences.zh: 遂出擊，大破之，追奔百里，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: He then went out to attack, inflicted a great defeat, pursued the fleeing enemy a hundred li, and captured or beheaded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He sallied forth, crushed them, chased them a hundred li, and took or killed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遼東孟暉，先沒於宇文部，帥其眾數千家降於廆，廆以為建威將軍。

translations.literal: Meng Hui of Liaodong had earlier been lost among the Wenyuan tribe; he led his following of several thousand families to surrender to Hui, and Hui made him General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hui of Liaodong, once lost among the Wenyuan, brought several thousand families to surrender. Hui made him general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 廆以其臣慕輿句勤恪廉靖，使掌府庫；

translations.literal: Hui, because his minister Murong Ju was diligent, honest, and quiet, had him manage the storehouses;
translations.idiomatic: Hui set Murong Ju, honest and steady, over the storehouses;

sentences.zh: 句心計默識，不案簿書，始終無漏。

translations.literal: Ju kept accounts in his mind and did not consult ledgers; from start to finish nothing leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Ju kept accounts in his head without opening ledgers, and nothing slipped through.

sentences.zh: 以慕輿河明敏精審，使典獄訟，覆訊清允。

translations.literal: He made Murong He bright, keen, and exacting, and had him oversee prisons and litigation; re-examination was clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He made the sharp-eyed Murong He oversee prisons. Retrials came out clear and fair.

translations.literal: category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
translations.idiomatic: category: Zizhi Tongjian
